title: Commanders to sign CB Fabian Moreau
summary: Cornerback Fabian Moreau is heading back to where he started his NFL career.
full_text: '' Cornerback Fabian Moreau is heading back to where he started his NFL career. Mike Garafolo of NFL Media reports that Moreau is signing with the Commanders. Washington drafted Moreau in the third round of the 2017 draft. Moreau spent four seasons with the team before moving on to stints with the Falcons, Texans, Giants, Broncos and Vikings. After playing for Minnesota in 2024, Moreau spent part of last summer with the 49ers and then returned to the Vikings after being cut in late August. Moreau had 17 tackles in 11 games last season. He has 322 tackles, five tackles for loss, seven interceptions, three forced fumbles and a fumble recovery over his entire career.
author: Josh Alper

title: Matthew Stafford: Practice is as high quality as I've been around
summary: The Rams opened up their offseason by making a pair of moves to improve their cornerback group and the impact was on display during Monday's practice.
full_text: The Rams opened up their offseason by making a pair of moves to improve their cornerback group and the impact was on display during Monday's practice. Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson had highlight moments by breaking up passes from Matthew Stafford to wideouts Davante Adams and Puka Nacua. The offense rebounded with touchdown passes to both receivers before the defense came up with more strong plays on a back-and-forth day at Rams camp. After it was over, Stafford said it was the best practice work he's seen since entering the NFL in 2009. "There was a a lot of high quality plays out there, plays that in the books will go down as good for the offense, and in the books it'll go down as good for the defense," Stafford said, via the team's website. "Sometimes you just tip your cap. . . . as high quality of practice football as I've been around." All of that played out without defensive end Myles Garrett on the field due to lower body soreness and adding him to the riches that were already on display makes it easy to understand why the Rams are one of the favorites heading into the 2026 season.
author: Josh Alper

title: John Harbaugh "very encouraged" by Arvell Reese's start to training camp
summary: The Giants had their first padded practice of the summer on Monday and one of the newest members of the team stood out during the session.
full_text: The Giants had their first padded practice of the summer on Monday and one of the newest members of the team stood out during the session. Reporters at the practice singled out first-round pick Arvell Reese as the main attraction. The linebacker stuffed running backs at the line, made plays in pass coverage and was credited with a sack of Jaxson Dart over the course of the sessions. That's the kind of multifaceted impact on defense that made Reese a prized prospect and it left head coach John Harbaugh singing the rookie's praises. "Very encouraged," Harbaugh said, via a transcript from the team. "I think he looked good today from what I could see. I can't wait to see the tape, but he's playing really well. He's been playing well the whole camp since he got here. . . . You see the talent, obviously. I think he's very sharp for a first-year guy. He gets things right pretty much all the time, makes very few mistakes. He's a very serious-minded guy, and he's very determined. I mean, he's doing things well." After the Giants picked Reese, there were questions about how the Giants would deploy him in their defense. They settled on using him as an off-ball linebacker, but the early days of training camp show that Reese could have a wide-ranging impact come the fall.
author: Josh Alper

title: With Jadeveon Clowney returning to Houston, Logan Hall gives up No. 90 jersey
summary: Jadeveon Clowney is returning to Houston, and teammate Logan Hall has apparently given him the No. 90 jersey.
full_text: ''' Jadeveon Clowney is returning to Houston, and teammate Logan Hall has apparently given him the No. 90 jersey. Hall, who signed with the Texans this offseason after playing his first four NFL seasons for the Buccaneers, had been wearing No. 90 in Houston just as he did in Tampa Bay. But the Texans announced that Hall is now wearing No. 96. There's been no formal announcement that Clowney will wear No. 90, but Hall presumably gave up No. 90 so that Clowney could have it. Clowney wore No. 90 from 2014, when the Texans made him the first overall pick in the NFL draft, until 2019, when he was traded to Seattle and played one season for the Seahawks. Clowney also wore No. 90 for two seasons with the Browns, but he has worn other numbers in other places: No. 99 for the Titans, No. 24 for the Ravens, No. 7 for the Panthers and No. 42 for the Cowboys. Now that he's back to Houston, he's back to his original Texans jersey, one that plenty of Texans fans still have and will wear again this season. And Hall will generate some good will in Houston for a gesture of respect to a player who wore No. 90 before him.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Andy Reid: Mia Bieniemy is improving every day, no timetable for Eric to return
summary: Mia Bieniemy, the wife of Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy, is improving after she was shot in their home in Virginia on July 26.
full_text: Mia Bieniemy, the wife of Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy, is improving after she was shot in their home in Virginia on July 26. Although Mia Bieniemy remains hospitalized, she is doing better, according to Chiefs coach Andy Reid, who said Eric Bieniemy remains away from the team with no scheduled return. "On the Eric Bieniemy side, Mia's doing better, she keeps improving by the day, so that's a positive. There's no timetable on EB coming back or any of that. He just needs to take care of business and when he gets back here he gets back here," Reid said. Eric and Mia's son Elijah Bieniemy was arrested and charged with malicious wounding, use of a firearm in commission of a felony and discharge of a firearm inside a dwelling in connection with the shooting. Elijah Bieniemy has been jailed since then. Court appearances have been delayed while Elijah undergoes mental health evaluations.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Penei Sewell: Dan Campbell sets a standard, if you don't meet it you're not a Detroit Lion
summary: "That's the mindset, I have to be the best today, be the greatest today," Sewell said.
full_text: Lions left tackle Penei Sewell says every player on the 90-man training camp roster understands exactly what is expected of anyone who's going to be a Lion when the regular season starts. Asked what head coach Dan Campbell emphasizes to the players, Sewell said Campbell lets everyone know there are high standards that have to be met if you want to be a member of this team. "It’s the standard, in everything that you do, from the way it’s taught to the way it’s done, how it’s done, what, why, everything. There’s no gray area. It’s either you do or you don’t, and if you don’t then you’re not a Detroit Lion," Sewell said. Sewell has moved to the left side after previously playing right tackle, and he said the standard for himself is to play left tackle at the highest level from Day One. "That's the mindset, I have to be the best today, be the greatest today," Sewell said. Sewell was the Lions' first draft pick during Campbell's tenure as head coach, and the two of them are on the same page about setting high standards, for themselves and for the franchise.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Kyle Juszczyk: Deebo Samuel is the best, incredible teammate, excited to have him back
summary: "His first day in pads he's making an impact right way. He just looked like the old Deebo," Juszczyk said.
full_text: After one year in Washington, wide receiver Deebo Samuel has returned to San Francisco. And 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk couldn't be happier about that. Juszczyk, who was in San Francisco for all six of Samuel's seasons on the 49ers, said that Samuel was a great teammate in the past and is already showing that he's a great teammate again. “Deebo’s the best. He’s such an incredible teammate. He’s such a good friend. He’s an incredible football player," Juszczyk said. "So we’re really happy to have him in the locker room just because he brings the best vibes, and positivity, but we’re also happy to have him on the field because he’s still got juice and he can still go out there and make big plays. He came in, he looks like he’s in phenomenal shape. His first day in pads he's making an impact right way. He just looked like the old Deebo, so I can't say enough positive things about how excited we are to have him." The 49ers traded Samuel to the Commanders last year, and when he returned to the 49ers last week, he said it felt like he never left . Juszczyk agrees.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Steelers on Aaron Rodgers: "Our players are entitled to their own personal views"
summary: Monday's rollicking, grievance-airing appearance by Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers on The Pat McAfee Show prompted ESPN, one of the targets of Rodgers's ire, to say nothing.
full_text: Monday's r ollicking, grievance-airing appearance by Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers on The Pat McAfee Show prompted ESPN, one of the targets of Rodgers's ire, to say nothing . The Steelers issued a comment essentially supporting Rodgers's ability to say whatever he wants, whenever he wants, wherever he wants. "Discussions around culture and politics can bring differing perspectives, and our players are entitled to their own personal views ," Steelers spokesman Burt Lauten told WTAE-TV, via Steelers Depot . "With respect to that, I am certain there are a variety of opinions on many topics within our locker room." It's an accurate observation, but the real question is what does coach Mike McCarthy think about it? Coaches loathe distractions, and Rodgers gratuitously created one on Monday. Last year, Rodgers didn't appear once on McAfee's show during the season, breaking from a habit of showing up on Tuesdays and, from time to time, spouting off on all sorts of things that prompted scrutiny and criticism. It doesn't take a genius (which qualifies me for the job) to conclude that former Steelers coach Mike Tomlin found a way to persuade Rodgers to restrict his 2025 media appearances to the league-required midweek and post-game press conferences. Tomlin lived it with former Steelers quarterback Ben Roethlisberger, whose prior habit of making weekly appearances on 93.7 The Fan in Pittsburgh created periodic issues that kept Tomlin from fully focusing on the task of preparing his team to win football games. Eventually, and possibly at Tomlin's suggestion, Roethlisberger stopped doing it. If Tomlin were still the coach in Pittsburgh, would Rodgers have gone scorched earth on Dr. Anthony Fauci and ESPN? Probably not.
author: Mike Florio

title: Notre Dame-USC rivalry returns in 2030, for at least four years
summary: One of the greatest rivalries in college football won't happen this year, exactly one century after USC and Notre Dame first played.
full_text: One of the greatest rivalries in college football won't happen this year, exactly one century after USC and Notre Dame first played. They'll pick it up again in 2030. Via Ryan Kartje of the L.A. Times , the Trojans and the Irish have agreed on a four-year home-and-home arrangement beginning in four years. The series fell apart because USC wanted to move it earlier in the year. Notre Dame resisted. In the end, the first two games in 2030 and 2031 will be played in Week 1, with the 2030 contest at the L.A. Coliseum and the 2031 showdown at South Bend. The 2032 and 2033 editions will land between Week 1 and Week 3. After 2033, they'll have to agree to continue. Hopefully, they will. Too many great rivalries have been lost in recent decades, as conferences have constantly expanded and shifted and created all sorts of odd matchups that defy the traditions that make college football great. For the next four seasons, it'll be a little less great without an annual Notre Dame vs. USC game. Come 2030, it will return — for at least four years and hopefully for a lot longer.
author: Mike Florio

title: Greg Olsen could be the eventual successor to Tony Romo
summary: Olsen can exit Fox contract for No. 1 spot elsewhere.
full_text: ' For now, J.J. Watt will replace Tony Romo on the top NFL broadcasting team at CBS. If Romo never returns, the job eventually could go to Greg Olsen. In the latest edition of his Varsity newsletter for Puck , John Ourand mentions Watt and Olsen as the two potential long-term replacements for Romo, in the event CBS moves on from Romo. The elephant in the room for CBS and Romo comes from the $72 million remaining on his contract, over the next four years. CBS could try to terminate the agreement with cause, owing Romo nothing. But that would invite a legal battle. The two sides could strike a settlement, in which Romo would get some of the money ($36 million would be half) and walk away. Olsen, as Ourand notes, has the ability to walk away from his Fox deal if he's offered the top spot at another network. Olsen had that position at Fox, until Fox hired Tom Brady. Why wouldn't CBS want Olsen? He has won three Emmys. Earlier this year, Olsen bested Brady for Outstanding Personality/Event Analyst. The first step is whether Romo's leave will be temporary or permanent. The current signs point to Romo having a steep uphill climb to stick around, punctuated by the terse, one-sentence release announcing that he'll be on leave "until further notice." If Romo is indeed gone for good, Watt and Olsen could be the two names to watch.
author: Mike Florio

title: Nick Foles, Clay Matthews join Netflix studio show for the Week 1 game in Australia
summary: The Netflix lineup for next month's 49ers-Rams game has been finalized.
full_text: ' The Netflix lineup for next month's 49ers-Rams game has been finalized. Netflix announced on Monday that Nick Foles and Clay Matthews will join the studio show for the Week 1 game in Australia, along with host Elle Duncan and analyst Michael Irvin. While the announcement focuses only on the first game, it's possible if not likely that Foles and Matthews will be back for the other four 2026 Netflix games. Duncan has said that Netflix will have a consistent studio presence for all of its games this season. Working the 49ers-Rams game will be Noah Eagle and Luke Kuechly, with former NFL Network host MJ Acosta serving as the reporter. Again, it's likely we'll see and hear the same trio for the Thanksgiving Eve game, one of the two Christmas games, and the Netflix Week 18 Saturday game. After streaming Christmas games in 2024 and 2025, Netflix expanded its footprint to five annual games on a deal that runs through 2029. Although Netflix has said it doesn't want a full-season package, many things can and will change over the next four years.
author: Mike Florio

title: Cowboys TE Princeton Fant carted off with knee injury
summary: Cowboys tight end Princeton Fant was carted off from Monday's practice after an apparent left knee injury.
full_text: ' Cowboys tight end Princeton Fant was carted off from Monday's practice after an apparent left knee injury. Calvin Watkins of the Dallas Morning News reports Fant was scheduled for an MRI to determine the extent of the injury. The Cowboys also have Jake Ferguson, Brevyn Spann-Ford and Luke Schoonmaker at the position. Fant took a knee-to-knee hit after being blocked backward into running back Israel Abanikanda during the Cowboys' first padded practice of training camp. He was unable to put weight on his left leg, requiring a cart to leave the field. Fant signed with the Cowboys as an undrafted free agent out of Tennessee in 2023. He has appeared in 11 games in three seasons, playing mostly on special teams.
author: Charean Williams

title: Jerry Jones would be "open to" selling a minority share of Cowboys to Mark Cuban
summary: The man who once warned the NFL that "pigs get fat, hogs get slaughtered" could be looking for a spot at the trough.
full_text: ' The man who once warned the NFL that " pigs get fat, hogs get slaughtered " could be looking for a spot at the trough. Via Calvin Watkins of the Dallas Morning News , former Mavericks owner Mark Cuban says he's "open to" buying a piece of the Cowboys. And Cowboys owner Jerry Jones says he's "open to" selling one to Cuban. “That’s exactly why if you’re me, you would be open to that is because of the man,” Jones told Watkins. “I have all the respect in the world for him and I know what he did for the Mavericks and what he’s done for basketball. He’s in additional to financial boatstreams of your team, you want to associate with the highest quality of [a person] who loves the game and then also at the same time wants to do something about it. Mark leads the way in that.” “I’m sure our Harbinger fund would be open to it,” Cuban told Watkins on the possibility of buying an interest in the Cowboys. The Harbinger fund, however, isn't one of the private-equity funds approved to buy slices of NFL teams. Besides, Jones may want Cuban as a partner, not Cuban's private-equity fund. The conversation apparently arises from recent comments from Cowboys executive Stephen Jones regarding the possibility of selling a minority stake in the team. But being "open to" the possibility and turning it into a done deal are two different things. Jones may want much more than Cuban would pay, for example. Cuban made his prediction that the NFL was 10 years away from implosion in 2014. Since then, franchise values have exploded. And there's no end in sight. Earlier this year, Jones provided the best response possible to Cuban's pigs/hogs line: " When the ducks quack, feed ‘em ." The simple reality is that the ducks keep quacking, as loud as ever. And the pigs turned hogs will eventually grow into a new species that's bigger than any other porcine creature that ever walked the earth. And Cuban apparently had realized, as to the NFL, that if you can't beat 'em, feed 'em.
author: Mike Florio

title: Todd Monken: Dillon Gabriel is earning more reps
summary: In the Cleveland quarterback competition between Shedeur Sanders and Deshaun Watson, there could be a third candidate creeping up on the outside.
full_text: In the Cleveland quarterback competition between Shedeur Sanders and Deshaun Watson, there could be a third candidate creeping up on the outside. Dillon Gabriel, drafted two rounds before Sanders in 2025, is performing well enough to earn more chances to perform. "I said it the other day, everybody’s competing, but you’re not guaranteed the same amount of reps," coach Todd Monken told reporters on Monday. "So it’s up to the player to take advantage and maximize those reps, which I feel like Dillon has done. So we’ll see as we move forward, if that continues, we’ll continue to up his reps. He’s earned that. That’s what every player should expect, right? If they play well, you have to up the reps, or what’s the purpose of playing well?” The best players play. If neither Sanders nor Watson seize the job and Gabriel continues to do the most with the chances he has, why shouldn't he get more chances? In theory, that could mean stealing the job from both of them — if he ends up being the best performer of the bunch. Gabriel started six games in 2025, replacing Week 1 starter Joe Flacco. After going 1-5 in those games, Gabriel yielded to Sanders. And so the forgotten man on the depth chart could be forcing the Browns to remember him. And, eventually, to play him.
author: Mike Florio

title: Cardinals DT Walter Nolen is healthy and motivated
summary: The Cardinals drafted defensive tackle Walter Nolen with the 16th overall pick in 2025.
full_text: '' The Cardinals drafted defensive tackle Walter Nolen with the 16th overall pick in 2025. He played six games with no starts and totaled 11 tackles, two sacks and five quarterback hits. " I don’t feel like I did enough ," Nolen said, via Darren Urban of the team website. "Being healthy is a big part of it." Nolen had a calf injury early and a meniscus tear in his left knee late. He was limping on the sideline during Friday's practice, but Nolen is healthy. “I’m great. It was just a little hiccup,” Nolen said. “We got a long season ahead, so just doing what’s best for me. I’m faithful in the work that I put in. I’m faithful in the Lord, and I feel like everything good.” Nolen dropped 10 pounds in the offseason by giving up junk food. He said he feels "more explosive" than last season. The Cardinals are counting on him being more productive, too. "I can't say I've been on a good football team that didn't have a very good defensive line, that wreaked havoc," coach Mike LaFleur said.
author: Charean Williams

title: Jaylen Warren: First day of practice in pads was "most tame, uneventful" he's seen
summary: Things are very different in Latrobe.
full_text: Things are very different in Latrobe. On the first day of practice in pads with a head coach other than Mike Tomlin in twenty years, the pads weren't popping like they used to. “That was the most tame, uneventful first day in pads I’ve seen in all my years at training camp,” running back Jaylen Warren told reporters after practice, via Nathan Schivins of the Latrobe Bulletin . Warren, in his fifth Steelers training camp, said that it was "not what we're used to." It's the latest example of the manner in which new coach Mike McCarthy is balancing player health with preparedness. Eyebrows initially were raised when McCarthy said last week that the Steelers will not tackle to the ground. The fundamental differences between training-camp intensity will surely be cited as the biggest difference between the two Mikes, in the event a franchise that never had a losing record under Tomlin finds itself under .500 when the dust settles on the 2026 season.
author: Mike Florio

title: Rams TE Davis Allen to miss "some time" with quad injury
summary: The Rams are going to be short a tight end for a little while.
full_text: The Rams are going to be short a tight end for a little while. Head coach Sean McVay told reporters on Monday that Davis Allen is going to miss "some time" as he recovers from a quad injury. McVay said the team does not want to rush Allen back because of their plans for him this season. "Davis is going to be a big part of what we do," McVay said, via Stu Jackson of the team's website. Allen played in every game for the Rams last season and made six starts. He had 24 catches for 208 yards and three touchdowns in the regular season. Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson, Terrance Ferguson, and second-round pick Max Klare remain on hand at tight end.
author: Josh Alper

title: ESPN has no comment on Aaron Rodgers's comments on ESPN, about ESPN
summary: On Monday, Aaron Rodgers had some strong things to say about ESPN.
full_text: On Monday, Aaron Rodgers had some strong things to say about ESPN. While appearing on ESPN. Per an ESPN spokesperson, ESPN has no comment regarding Rodgers's comments. Rodgers's rant initially focused on Dr. Anthony Fauci, as Rodgers did a COVID victory lap — one that glossed over the fact that Rodgers was disingenuous at best when he misled reporters in August 2021 on the question of whether he had received a vaccine. Rodgers then pivoted to ESPN, for not covering Fauci's repeated invocation of the Fifth Amendment at a Senate hearing last Thursday. (Should it have been the lead item on SportsCenter ?) “How much time did the network spend on that?” Rodgers said. “How much time do they spend on my responses every week? On my vaccination status, on Taylor [Swift] and Travis [Kelce’s] wedding? Did they do even a minute? Did they do even a minute on Tony Fauci? No, I bet they didn’t.” Rodgers also chastised ESPN for not covering the Mike Vrabel-Dianna Russini situation. “Then there was another scandal this offseason, too, involving a voter for MVP, for coach of the year,” Rodgers said. “How much time did your network spend on that? . . . Like, you have literally an individual that maybe used to work at ESPN that covers our league at the highest level, and there’s a major scandal, and it’s just, like, nobody can fucking talk about it. What are we even doing here? . . . [I]f it’s affecting certain things, if there’s leaks going on, if there’s tampering going on, if that person is also an MVP voter and a coach of the year voter.” While ESPN did cover it to an extent, it wasn't as big of a deal as it could have been. A thorough item from Ben Strauss was posted by ESPN.com on a Friday afternoon , with no corresponding car wash of interviews on the various ESPN shows. And ESPN has kept its head low and its mouth shut regarding the question of whether the relationship between Vrabel and Russini impacted her reporting while she worked for ESPN. Rodgers also accused ESPN of being a "gutless organization" with "no integrity." Last year, Rodgers ended his weekly Tuesday visits with Pat McAfee on ESPN. It will be very interesting to see whether Rodgers, in his final NFL season, resumes making the appearances — and whether he continues to air personal grievances and settle old scores. And whether he continues to take shots at the company that ultimately owns the platform, without any pushback from ESPN.
author: Mike Florio

title: Ravens have no deadline to name a starting center
summary: The Ravens aren't in any rush to name a starting center.
full_text: '' The Ravens aren't in any rush to name a starting center. They signed Ethan Pocic just before the start of camp and he is competing with Danny Pinter and Jovaughn Gwyn as the Ravens look for a new starter in the wake of Tyler Linderbaum's move to the Raiders in free agency. Pocic tore his Achilles last December, which head coach Jesse Minter cited as a reason why the team plans to take its time. "I don't know that there’s a deadline ," Minter said, via the team's website. "One of them in the mix of the battle is coming off of an injury. That timeline may or may not be perfect for that first game. There will come a point in time where we will certainly focus on getting ready for that first game. I think a couple weeks out, that will probably shake itself out." Pocic has the most starting experience of the trio and we'll find out if the extended time to compete for the job leads to him landing it before Week 1.
author: Josh Alper

title: Former Broncos, Dolphins, Raiders LB Jerry Wayne Hopkins dies at 85
summary: Former NFL linebacker Jerry Wayne Hopkins has died at 85.
full_text: '' Former NFL linebacker Jerry Wayne Hopkins has died at 85. His funeral was Monday in Hillsboro, Texas. (Hopkins is on the left in the photo.) He played center and linebacker at Texas A&M from 1960-62, earning first-team All-Southwest Conference honors in his final college season. Hopkins played in three college all-star games — Blue-Gray Game, the Southwest Challenge Bowl and the All-American Classic. The Houston Oilers selected Hopkins in the fourth round of the AFL draft in 1963. He played four seasons for the Broncos, one for the Dolphins and one for the Raiders. Hopkins had a team-leading eight sacks in 1964 with the Broncos. After his retirement, Hopkins owned and operated Hopkins Oil Company. He is survived by his wife, Joan Brooks Hopkins; his son, Jerry Hopkins, Jr. (Ali); his daughter, Allison Hopkins; his granddaughter, Parker Hopkins; and his sister, Judy Baker (Buddy).
author: Charean Williams

title: Ravens to sign OL Kendall Lamm
summary: The Ravens lost an experienced backup offensive lineman when Hakeem Adeniji retired, but they've found another one to take his spot on the roster.
full_text: '' The Ravens lost an experienced backup offensive lineman when Hakeem Adeniji retired , but they've found another one to take his spot on the roster. Jeff Zrebiec of TheAthletic.com reports that the Ravens are signing tackle Kendall Lamm. Lamm was one of three offensive linemen to work out for the team on Monday. Lamm has played for four teams since entering the league as an undrafted free agent in 2015. He spent the last four seasons in Miami and started 16 of the 46 games that he played for the Dolphins. Lamm has also played for the Titans, Browns and Texans. The NFL's daily transaction report shows that Jake Curhan and Nicholas Petit-Frere also worked out for the Ravens.
author: Josh Alper

title: Cardinals claim RB Evan Hull, DT Cam Horsley off waivers
summary: The Cardinals claimed two players off waivers on Monday, according to the NFL's personnel notice.
full_text: ' The Cardinals claimed two players off waivers on Monday, according to the NFL's personnel notice. Running back Evan Hull and defensive tackle Cam Horsley now are Cardinals. In corresponding moves, the Cardinals waived defensive tackle Coziah Izzard and wide receiver Tejhuan Palmer. The Texans released Hull, who was a fifth-round pick of the Colts in 2023. He also has spent time with the Steelers and Saints. In 2025, he appeared in six games for the Saints and rushed for 48 yards on 19 carries and caught one pass for 6 yards. He has played eight career games. Horsely signed with the Titans as an undrafted free agent in 2025 and appeared in one game as a rookie, playing 14 defensive snaps. The Titans waived him Sunday.
author: Charean Williams

title: Colts teammates say Daniel Jones looks like he never got hurt
summary: Colts quarterback Daniel Jones is coming off a torn Achilles tendon, but you wouldn't know that from seeing him at training camp.
full_text: '' Colts quarterback Daniel Jones is coming off a torn Achilles tendon, but you wouldn't know that from seeing him at training camp. That's the word from teammates, who say Jones looks as good as ever on the practice field. " He looks like he never got hurt ," tight end Mo Alie-Cox said, via Colts.com. "He's throwing dimes left and right on the field, getting out the pocket, scrambling and different things like that." Colts guard Quenton Nelson said Jones is doing everything he could do last season. "He's been incredible. He's back like he's never left," Nelson said. "He worked so hard to get here. It's been awesome to see." Until Jones is facing defenders who can hit him in live action, expectations should be tempered. But the early returns suggest he's on track to make the Achilles injury a distant memory when the Colts open the regular season against the Ravens on September 13.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Report: Mike Evans quad injury "could get resolved relatively quickly"
summary: The 49ers receiving corps has been hit by several injuries early on in camp, but one veteran may be back on the field sooner rather than later.
full_text: The 49ers receiving corps has been hit by several injuries early on in camp, but one veteran may be back on the field sooner rather than later. Ian Rapoport of NFL Network noted that Mike Evans' quad strain does not appear to be serious. "It does seem like something that could get resolved relatively quickly , just by the term 'strain,'" Rapoport said on Inside Training Camp Live, via David Bonilla of 49erswebzone.com. "It generally relates to a minor-type injury, and Mike Evans, he's been through training camps, been through a lot of training camps, certainly is someone who does not need the reps. They're going to give him probably a lighter load anyway, so I wouldn't be surprised if he misses some practice time. "I wouldn't be surprised if he is able to go sooner rather than later, but make no mistake, this has been one of the big storylines of their training camp.” Rapoport later referred to Evans’ injury as “not too serious, but certainly something we’re going to keep an eye on” when talking about the 49ers’ larger injury issues. San Francisco has already lost Ricky Pearsall for the season while De’Zhaun Stribling and Christian Kirk are also dealing with injuries. Evans signed a three-year deal with the 49ers as a free agent in March.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Sean Payton: No hurry with Taysom Hill, I'll see him in Canton this week
summary: Broncos head coach Sean Payton will be in Canton, Ohio this week to take part in Drew Brees's induction into the Pro Football Hall of Fame and he'll also do a little work on a possible addition to his roster.
full_text: Broncos head coach Sean Payton will be in Canton, Ohio this week to take part in Drew Brees's induction into the Pro Football Hall of Fame and he'll also do a little work on a possible addition to his roster. Payton said over the weekend that the Broncos will explore signing former Saints tight end Taysom Hill and Hill will also be in Canton for Brees's induction. That will give Payton a chance to see where things stand. "There's no hurry right now. I'm going to see him in five days ," Payton said Monday, via Jeff Legwold of ESPN.com. "We'll see where he's at and kind of go from there. ... The key thing is his health and, you know, where he's at mentally. I don't want to assume he wants to play." Hill released a statement last month saying that he doesn't "have a clear answer about what the future holds, but I know that returning to New Orleans is not in the cards." He had knee surgery in 2024 that was performed by the Broncos' team doctor Karim Meijer and Payton said that Meijer has followed up with Hill during visits in Denver since the operation.
author: Josh Alper

title: De'Von Achane aims to win the rushing title this season
summary: The Dolphins rewarded De'Von Achane after a 1,350-yard season, making him the third-highest-paid running back in yearly average.
full_text: The Dolphins rewarded De'Von Achane after a 1,350-yard season, making him the third-highest-paid running back in yearly average. His $16 million average trails only Saquon Barkley and Christian McCaffrey. His rushing yards last season ranked behind only James Cook, Derrick Henry, Jonathan Taylor and Bijan Robinson. Achane's goal for 2026 is to outrush them all. “For me, it’s trying to get the rushing title ," Achane told NFL Network on Sunday. "That’s something I want to do this year. I feel like if I got the rushing title, every game we’re doing something good. If we’re productive, if I’m being productive, helping my team win, I feel like as a whole, we’re doing something great. "We got a lot of new faces, so I feel like I got out there, I've got to lead, and I've got to show by example.” The Dolphins will lean heavily on Achane's legs after trading wide receiver Jaylen Waddle and releasing wide receiver Tyreek Hill. Achane led the league with a 5.7-yards-per-attempt average last season.
author: Charean Williams

title: Patriots sign DT Casey Rogers
summary: The Patriots announced an addition to their roster on Monday afternoon.
full_text: '' The Patriots announced an addition to their roster on Monday afternoon. They have signed defensive tackle Casey Rogers. There was no corresponding move needed because New England had an open spot after releasing linebacker Otis Reese late last week. Rogers played in two games for the Giants in 2024 and then joined the Bills last spring after being waived. He failed to make it through Buffalo's final cut and returned to the Giants practice squad. He played in one game and then moved on to play for the DC Defenders in the UFL this spring. Rogers had 21 tackles, two tackles for loss and 1.5 sacks during his time with the Defenders.
author: Josh Alper

title: Browns rookie WR KC Concepcion appears to injure right shoulder
summary: Browns rookie wide receiver KC Concepcion was injured in the 2-minute drill at the end of Monday's practice.
full_text: Browns rookie wide receiver KC Concepcion was injured in the 2-minute drill at the end of Monday's practice. He appeared to injure his right shoulder after landing on the turf on a hit by Myles Harden, according to multiple reports. Concepcion stayed on the ground before walking to the sideline with athletic trainers while holding his shoulder. Mary Kay Cabot of cleveland.com reports that Concepcion didn't go inside immediately. He remained on the field after practice and was talking to running backs Duce Staley and others, so it is unclear whether it was merely a scare. The Browns drafted Concepcion in the first round out of Texas A&M. He totaled 61 receptions for 919 yards and nine touchdowns and added two punt return touchdowns in his only season with the Aggies. In his three-year college career, which included two seasons at North Carolina State, Concepcion totaled 2,218 receiving yards, 431 rushing yards and 28 touchdowns from scrimmage.
author: Charean Williams

title: Quinn Ewers: We all want to play, but we all want what's best for the Dolphins
summary: When the Dolphins moved on from Tua Tagovailoa during the offseason, it briefly appeared second-year quarterback Quinn Ewers might have a chance to start in 2026.
full_text: When the Dolphins moved on from Tua Tagovailoa during the offseason, it briefly appeared second-year quarterback Quinn Ewers might have a chance to start in 2026. Ewers, after all, had started Miami’s last three games, helping pilot the club to a victory over the Buccaneers in Week 17. But then the Dolphins signed Malik Willis early in free agency, with the implication being that Willis would be the starter. That was no matter to the former Texas QB. “ I was excited to get to work with him, honestly ,” Ewers said on Monday of his reaction to Miami signing Willis, via David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel . “I think he had a great end of the year last year with Green Bay, and to get a guy like that who has played good in some big-time games is only going to help me in the long run.” So even as Ewers would like to have a shot at being QB1, he’s committed to being as helpful as possible for Willis and every other quarterback on the roster. “In the quarterback room, the respective goal is to be playing on Sundays, but I think that’s the cool part about our room,” Ewers said. “We all want to be playing, but at the end of the day, I think we all want what’s best for the Dolphins. So, we’re all competing for the same spot, but we’re all competing for the same goal. Whoever’s out there, no matter who it is, anybody’s going to get the support.” In his four total appearances, Ewers completed 66.3 percent of his passes for 622 yards with three touchdowns and three interceptions as a rookie in 2025.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Aaron Rodgers torches "Tony" Fauci and ESPN, while appearing on ESPN
summary: Rodgers relitigates COVID, chastises ESPN for not covering the Mike Vrabel-Dianna Russini scandal.
full_text: It really is a " full circle " year for Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers. At a time when Rodgers was seemingly creating a kinder, gentler vibe as he embarks on his final year in the NFL, Rodgers brought the knives out during a Monday appearance on ESPN's The Pat McAfee Show . Rodgers started by taking the Fifth Amendment in response to McAfee's first question. Rodgers then went off on Dr. Anthony Fauci, who last week repeatedly invoked the Fifth Amendment in testimony before the Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs. "You got a pardon, and you're in front of — and you pleaded [the Fifth] over 100 times?" Rodgers said. "What are you scared of, Tony? I thought you were the science. I thought you [were], 'I am science.' And you get up there and you can't answer a question?" The vitriol extended to ESPN, the owner of the channel on which he was appearing. "How much time did the network spend on that?" Rodgers said. "How much time do they spend on my responses every week? On my vaccination status, on Taylor [Swift] and Travis [Kelce's] wedding? Did they do even a minute? Did they do even a minute on Tony Fauci? No, I bet they didn't." Rodgers then made reference to ESPN's conspicuously scant coverage of the Mike Vrabel-Dianna Russini situation. "Then there was another scandal this offseason, too, involving a voter for MVP, for coach of the year," Rodgers said. "How much time did your network spend on that?" Later in the segment (after it migrated from ESPN to YouTube only), Rodgers returned to the Russini story. "Like, you have literally an individual that maybe used to work at ESPN that covers our league at the highest level, and there's a major scandal, and it's just, like, nobody can fucking talk about it," Rodgers said. "What are we even doing here? . . . [I]f it's affecting certain things, if there's leaks going on, if there's tampering going on, if that person is also an MVP voter and a coach of the year voter." Rodgers also referred to ESPN as a "gutless organization" with "no integrity." As to Fauci, Rodgers eventually called him "an absolute criminal" while repeatedly labeling him an "absolute coward." (Rodgers at one point suggested that Fauci's wife is Ghislaine Maxwell's sister, before adding "allegedly.") Here's the part where I say some things about what Rodgers said. First, Rodgers is right about ESPN looking the other way on the Russini-Vrabel story. It's still not clear why that happened. Given that the relationship (whatever it was) between Russini and Vrabel apparently existed during Russini's time with ESPN, and to the extent it tainted her work ( e.g. , the 2021 reporting prior to the Julio Jones trade ), ESPN prefers not to peer down that rabbit hole. What did the producers know about the situation, and did they perhaps welcome the benefits it generated for Bristol? Those questions haven't been asked by ESPN, and surely won't be. Second, as to Fauci's decision to repeatedly invoke the Fifth Amendment, Rodgers doesn't seem to realize that Fauci's pardon wouldn't apply to any effort to paint anything he said last week as perjury. Considering some of the specious (to say the least) prosecutions that have been attempted by the current administration, anything Fauci said could have been called perjury. Even if it wasn't. “The only conclusion I can reach is that the sole reason he is calling me before this committee is to get me to say something — anything — that could vindicate his repeated public pledges that I end up, in his words — quote — ‘behind bars,’” Fauci said in his opening remarks to the committee run by Senator Rand Paul (R-Ky.). Third, Rodgers did not mention the one specific thing that caused him to attract the ire of many in 2021. In August of that year, Rodgers publicly lied about being vaccinated. Well, he didn't lie per se . He played a deliberate word game about being "immunized," forcing someone to ask a followup question about whether "immunized" means "vaccinated." (The followup question wasn't asked.) Rodgers had every right to not be vaccinated. He wanted to avoid the protocols the league developed (right or wrong) for unvaccinated players, including wearing a mask during press conferences. (Rodgers didn't wear one during the press conference when he claimed he was "immunized.") If he hadn't tested positive in November 2021, the hair-splitting never would have come to light. It's kind of amazing that folks are relitigating the fog-of-war niceties of a pandemic that killed more than a million Americans, and which prompted people to say and do all sorts of things (including a suggestion by a fairly influential person to inject bleach) in an effort to get it under control. The issue has been dusted off for one reason: To motivate voters who may be inclined to stay home for the upcoming midterm election, due to growing apathy and/or flat-out antipathy regarding the person who mused about bleach as a potential treatment for the virus. Bottom line? Rodgers's decision to take the high road as to his family is hardly an indication that he has fully committed to that path. On Monday, Rodgers took an extended jog on the low road — to the likely dismay of the executives at ESPN who had to hold their breath and count the seconds until it all finally ended.
author: Mike Florio

title: Bears' Ben Johnson compares Luther Burden III's mentality, approach to one of the NFL's best wide receivers
summary: Johnson says Burden has a desire to be great
full_text:
Chicago Bears coach Ben Johnson is widely considered one of the top offensive minds in the NFL . He's credited with engineering a significant step forward for last year's Bears offense, obviously, but before that, he was the offensive coordinator in Detroit, where he helped the Lions become one of the best offenses in football.
During that time, wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown developed into one of the best in the league at his position, catching at least 100 passes for at least 1,100 yards in each of Johnson's three seasons at the helm and earning a monster contract extension that made him among the highest-paid receivers in the league.
These days, Johnson coaches another receiver who he says has similarities to the Lions' star -- at least in terms of his approach on a day-to-day basis: second-year wideout Luther Burden III .
"St. Brown in Detroit, who I have a strong affinity for, he plays the game the same way," Johnson said during an interview with FOX32 . "I feel that from Luther. I know he wasn't a full-time starter for us a year ago, but the snaps that he did have, he's got that competitive edge and desire to be great."
As Johnson noted, Burden was not a full-time starter for the Bears last season. He wasn't a full-time player at all. Burden started just five of his 15 games and only played 40% of the team's offensive snaps, working behind D.J. Moore, Rome Odunze and even Olamide Zaccheaus for most of the season. Still, he caught 47 passes for 652 yards as a second-round pick. He also finished third in the NFL in yards per route run among the 152 wide receivers who ran at least 100 routes, according to Tru Media.
That type of efficiency on low volume is typically the kind of thing that leads to a dramatic increase in opportunity in the future, and it's clear that the Bears have big plans for Burden going forward, especially with their coach already comparing his work ethic to that of one of the game's best.
When it comes to playing style and usage, there are some similarities between Burden and St. Brown, but they're certainly not identical players.
For example, St. Brown (47%) was utilized in the slot more often than Burden (39%), despite the fact that Burden came into the league as primarily a slot receiver at Missouri. Still, just as he was in college, Burden was used primarily as a manufactured-touch player during his rookie season, with 32 of his 60 targets (53%) coming within five yards of the line of scrimmage. For St. Brown, that number was 69 of 172 targets (40%). St. Brown did more work in the intermediate area of the field (56.5% to 37%), while Burden got more downfield usage, with 6 of his 60 targets (10%) coming at least 20 yards past the line of scrimmage, while the same was true of just 6 of St. Brown's 172 targeted passes (3.5%).
To become the same type of impact player that St. Brown is, Burden will have to expand beyond the all-or-nothing type of usage he had last season. Being able to win and dominate on those intermediate routes is the key to unlocking NFL offenses, and especially an offense like Johnson's that specializes in getting players open in that 10-to-20-yard range.
St. Brown is already among the best in the league at winning in that area of the field, and that's why he dominates annually. Burden has a lot of talent, but he also has to prove that he can do more than just catch-and-run on designed touches or burn defenses with deep shots as he did on occasion last year. The Bears clearly think he can. The rest of us are waiting with bated breath to find out if they're right.
author: Jared Dubin

title: Bears lose Coby Bryant for 8-10 weeks after training camp knee injury
summary: Bryant suffered a hyperextended knee, bone bruise and small fracture during Monday's training camp practice
full_text:
Bears safety Coby Bryant will miss the next 8-10 weeks due to a hyperextended knee, bone bruise and small fracture suffered in Monday's training camp practice, ESPN reports . He is not expected to need surgery.
Bryant, 27, had to be carted off after going down during a one-on-one drill, per Adam Hoge .
Chicago signed Bryant, formerly of the Seahawks, to a three-year, $40 million deal this offseason, hoping to fortify its secondary with 2025 starting safeties Kevin Byard and Jaquan Brisker, both free agents. Byard signed with the Patriots , Brisker with the Steelers .
A fourth-round pick out of Cincinnati in 2022, Bryant thrived when Mike Macdonald arrived in Seattle in 2024 and moved him from cornerback to safety. Over the past two seasons, Bryant recorded seven interceptions (and returned one for a touchdown), 139 tackles, 13 passes defended, two forced fumbles and one fumble recovery. He started all 15 games he appeared in last season, as well as all three of the Seahawks ' playoff games en route to their Super Bowl triumph.
Chicago drafted Oregon safety Dillon Thieneman 25th overall in April, and he is likely to start at one safety spot. Cam Lewis could be next up to take Bryant's starting spot early in the season.
The Bears open their 2026 season on Sept. 13 -- less than six weeks away -- against the Panthers .
This is a significant loss for the Bears in more ways than one.
First, Bryant, the player, is an ascending talent with a nose for the football, the speed and agility to cover, and the strength to really thump opposing pass catchers and runners. His versatility is a sign of where the game is going at the safety position. According to Pro Football Focus, Bryant played the vast majority of his snaps (908 to be exact) at free safety last year, including playoffs, but he also played 177 snaps as a box safety and 60 snaps as a slot cornerback.
The Bears finished 29th in yards allowed per play last year, but survived thanks in large part to a league-leading 33 turnovers forced. Coach Ben Johnson and defensive coordinator Dennis Allen were certainly looking forward to having more down-to-down success and not having to rely so heavily on turnovers -- which can be finicky year over year -- and Bryant was a big part of that.
Second, the Bears are already thin in the secondary. Safety Elijah Hicks is on the PUP list with a shin injury, and standout nickel back Kyler Gordon is also on the PUP due to a calf injury that has had him sidelined all offseason. It's been a frustrating run for Gordon, who played in just five games, including the playoffs, last year due to calf and groin issues.
"Obviously, he's frustrated," general manager Ryan Poles said. "We're frustrated."
C.J. Gardner-Johnson, who played significant snaps for Chicago last year, joined the Bills this offseason. Behind Bryant, Thieneman, Hicks and Lewis on the depth chart are either undrafted rookies or journeymen who haven't played much. It makes sense that Chicago could pursue outside help.
Week 1: at Panthers Week 2: vs. Vikings Week 3: vs. Eagles (MNF) <-- exactly eight weeks away (early end of Bryant's injury return timeline) Week 4: vs. Jets Week 5: at Packers <-- nine weeks and six days away Week 6: at Falcons
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Justin Herbert found peace off the field. Mike McDaniel could bring it to the Chargers offense
summary: Fresh off his engagement to Madison Beer, Herbert is embracing a faster offense that could help him take fewer hits and elevate the Chargers in 2026
full_text:
A relationship with the right person can bring someone peace. Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert is experiencing that in two ways this offseason.
He got engaged to singer Madison Beer within the last week, and doing so has changed Herbert's life forever off the football field.
"It's hard to explain. It's been so incredible, and she's changed my life. It's something I never thought was possible. It's so awesome to find your person and be able to spend your life with them," Herbert said to SiriusXM on Saturday. "I'm excited and just can't wait. She's the best. ... It's what I've always dreamed of. Having someone I can share everything with, live with and trust completely. There's no better feeling."
On the football field, Herbert's partnership with new Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, who comes to Los Angeles after spending the last four seasons as the head coach of the Miami Dolphins , could provide Herbert with what he's always dreamed of on the field: peace.
Herbert and his cannon of a right arm have produced plenty of highlight-reel plays, as the two-time Pro Bowler's 24,820 passing yards through his first six NFL seasons rank second in NFL history through six years, trailing only Pro Football Hall of Famer Peyton Manning's 24,885.
However, Herbert has also been the NFL's most-sacked (225 times) and most-hit (615 times) quarterback since being drafted sixth overall in the 2020 NFL Draft . Those totals include a Chargers single-season record of 54 sacks taken in 2025, when he was also the league's most-pressured (263 times) and most-hit (129 times) quarterback.
Some of those eye-popping pressure numbers from 2025 can be attributed to Herbert's starting offensive tackles -- two-time Pro Bowl left tackle Rashawn Slater (ruptured patellar tendon in training camp, missed entire season) and Pro Bowl right tackle Joe Alt (missed 11 games with an ankle injury) -- being hit about as hard as they could be by the injury bug. Some of the overarching career numbers can also be attributed to the long-developing pass concepts of McDaniel's predecessor, Greg Roman.
Under Roman the last two seasons, the Chargers had the sixth-highest quarterback pressure rate allowed (38.1%) and the fifth-longest average time to throw (3.06 seconds). McDaniel's Dolphins offenses surrendered the NFL's second-lowest quarterback pressure rate (29.5%) while averaging the league's fastest time to throw (2.67 seconds) across his four seasons in charge from 2022-25.
Average time to throw (seconds)
McDaniel honed his offensive philosophy while working under Mike (2011-13 in Washington) and Kyle Shanahan (2006-08 in Houston, 2011-13 in Washington, 2014 in Cleveland, 2015-16 in Atlanta and 2017-21 in San Francisco). He learned their system of using similar under-center looks bolstered by zone-blocking schemes, heavy motion usage and play-action passing to make life easier for their quarterbacks.
In his first two seasons as Miami's head coach and offensive play-caller from 2022-23, McDaniel's Dolphins offenses averaged an NFL-best 6.3 yards per play with healthy seasons from quarterback Tua Tagovailoa and wide receiver Tyreek Hill. Despite the drop-off because of injuries to both players over the final two years, Miami still averaged 5.8 yards per play across McDaniel's four seasons, the fifth-most in the league during that span.
Now, McDaniel is asking Herbert to get the offense in and out of the huddle quickly, use motion (McDaniel's offenses averaged an NFL-high 73.6% motion rate from 2022-25) and trust the pass concepts built off their core sets and run-game action to get the football out of his right hand faster than ever.
That's why the Chargers are using training camp as Herbert's crash course in the new scheme and as an opportunity to increase his willingness to take risks. Doing so now could build the trust Herbert needs to let it rip come Week 1 against the Arizona Cardinals on Sept. 13.
"A lot of things I'm asking him to do take him out of his comfort zone, meaning guys with arm talent like he has, such a strong arm and great field vision, you want to protect the ball and want to confirm something before you throw it," McDaniel said Friday, via the team website .
"I'm challenging him to expedite that process and not confirm and let his feet talk to him and rip the ball. There were a couple times, one in particular on a throw to Ladd [McConkey], where he expressed to me today, 'Yeah, I was a little nervous throwing it that early.' But that's where you grow. In the front stages, I'm not worried about completion percentage. I'm not worried about picks, I'm worried about exposing yourself and challenging yourself."
So far, Herbert appears to be on board as he adjusts to a brand-new post-snap tempo.
"It's good. ... There were a few reps today where you're playing in timing, and they're getting the ball where they have the opportunity to turn upfield and make something happen," Herbert said on the first day of training camp . "You always want to avoid throwing late over the middle and throwing them into a defender. Any time I can get Q [ Quentin Johnston ] or Brenen [Brenen Thompson], any of those guys, opportunities to turn upfield, which I thought we did a couple times today. It was good to see, just playing fast and getting the ball out as quickly as I can."
Another upgrade for Herbert is a new offensive line. Los Angeles' 2026 offensive front features healthy versions of Slater and Alt, 2026 second-round pick Jake Slaughter slotting in at left guard, Pro Bowl center Tyler Biadasz arriving from Washington in free agency and former New England Patriots first-round pick Cole Strange filling the right guard spot.
Once Herbert and company find comfort in McDaniel's system, the quarterback could find a similar peace on the field to the one he's found off it. That type of peace could propel the Chargers to newfound postseason success just in time for a season in which Super Bowl LXI will be held on their home turf at SoFi Stadium.
"Listening to any advice he's got for me," Herbert said of McDaniel. "He's got a great feel for the position and the offense. He's been such an honor to work with."
author: Garrett Podell

title: NFL coach rankings are here, plus QB battle predictions and our top 100 players ever
summary: Here's everything you need to know about the NFL for Aug. 3
full_text:
Hello football friends, and welcome to the Monday edition of the Pick Six newsletter!
I'm not sure how it's possible, but there is actually going to be a football game this week. This is not a drill. I repeat: There is going to be an actual football game this week.
As of today, we're just three days away from the first game of the NFL preseason . It all kicks off Thursday when the Cardinals face the Panthers in the Hall of Fame Game, and although I'm sure those two teams will be excited to kick off the 2026 preseason, I have some bad news for their fan bases: No team has ever played in the Hall of Fame Game and gone on to win the Super Bowl that same season. Of course, the Cardinals and Panthers have never won a Super Bowl, so maybe that won't bother them.
Anyway, before we get to Thursday's game, we have a lot of ground to cover, so let's get to today's rundown.
As always, here's your daily reminder to tell all your friends to sign up for the newsletter. To get them signed up, all you have to do is click here .
Last week, we wrapped things up by ranking the top 10 players at every position in the NFL , and this week, we're kicking things off with another top 10 ranking: the league's best head coaches.
Here's how we came up with the rankings: We had 12 of our NFL experts cast ballots, with each voter submitting a personal top 10. A coach received 10 points for a first-place vote, nine points for second place and so on, down to one point for a 10th-place vote.
After all the votes were tallied, I learned one thing: The NFC West is absolutely loaded with top-tier head coaches.
Here are the top five names in our rankings:
1. Sean McVay ( Rams ) 2. Mike Macdonald ( Seahawks ) 3. Kyle Shanahan ( 49ers ) 4. Andy Reid ( Chiefs ) 5. Sean Payton ( Broncos )
If you read our full story, you'll not only see the full top 10, but you'll also see how the voting broke down. For instance, McVay was ranked first or second on all 12 ballots. On the other hand, Reid was ranked as low as seventh and as high as second, and he didn't receive a single first-place vote.
You're definitely going to want to check out our full rankings, and you can do that here .
Now that the first week of training camp is in the books, it's time for the good stuff. Things should start heating up this week, especially when it comes to the biggest QB battles around the league. There likely won't be any winners decided this week, but we could see the frontrunners begin to separate themselves with a strong week of practice.
There are currently four QB battles around the league -- Browns , Vikings , Falcons and Raiders -- and Tyler Sullivan broke down all of them. Let's check out his predictions for the battles in Cleveland and Minnesota:
NOTE: Although Sullivan is predicting Watson will win this battle, Garrett Podell recently laid out what Shedeur needs to do to steal the job, and you can check that out there .
If you want a breakdown of the QB battles in Atlanta and Las Vegas, we've got those here .
With Myles Garrett joining the Rams this offseason, it certainly feels like Los Angeles now has the best pass-rushing room in the NFL. Just to be sure, Carter Bahns decided to rank all 32 pass-rushing rooms, and yep, the Rams landed at the top.
If you want to win in the NFL, it certainly helps to have a good pass rush, so the Rams are in good shape. That's not the case for every team, though. With that in mind, let's check out the bottom three teams in Carter's rankings:
As I said at the top, Bahns ranked all 32 teams, and if you want to see his full list, you can do that here .
For the first time in NFL history, there's going to be a game in Australia. One reason it took so long for the NFL to head Down Under is because of the travel logistics. For the first time, two NFL teams will cross the international date line to play a regular-season game.
The 49ers and Rams will kick off at 10:35 a.m. on Friday, Sept. 11, in Australia, which will actually be an 8:35 p.m. ET kickoff on Thursday in the United States thanks to the 14-hour time difference between Melbourne and the Eastern time zone. The time change will be even more dramatic for the 49ers and Rams because Melbourne is 17 hours ahead of the Pacific time zone, where both teams are based.
This could be a game where the team with the better travel plan gains a small edge, which makes things especially interesting because the 49ers and Rams have completely different philosophies on how they'll handle the trip.
Let's take a look at each team's travel plan:
If you want the full breakdown of each team's plan, you can check that out here .
We wanted to make sure everyone had something fun to argue about to start August, so we decided to rank the top 100 players in NFL history.
Our resident historian, Bryan DeArdo, handled the rankings, and I have to say I agree with his entire list except for who he has at Nos. 24, 33, 71 and 98. Just kidding. I randomly came up with those numbers.
This list is actually pretty solid, and DeArdo crushed it, especially with the top 10.
TOP 10 PLAYERS IN NFL HISTORY
1. QB Tom Brady 2. WR Jerry Rice 3. RB Jim Brown 4. RB Walter Payton 5. QB Joe Montana 6. QB Peyton Manning 7. LB Lawrence Taylor 8. DE Reggie White 9. RB Barry Sanders 10. QB Dan Marino
The highest-ranked active player is Aaron Rodgers at No. 11. Patrick Mahomes came in right behind Rodgers at No. 12. Mahomes is entering just his 10th season, so there's plenty of time for him to crack the top 10, and maybe even climb higher, before he retires.
You can see our full top 100 list here .
It's been a busy few days around the NFL, and since it's nearly impossible to keep track of everything, I put together a quick roundup for you.
author: John Breech

title: Aaron Rodgers' preseason revenge tour could be coming: Steelers QB might play games vs. Packers and Jets
summary: Steelers coach Mike McCarthy wants the 42-year-old quarterback on the field for matchups against his former teams, but is the injury risk worth it?
full_text:
It's starting to look like the final season of Aaron Rodgers' NFL career is going to start off with a preseason revenge tour. The 42-year-old quarterback doesn't usually play in the preseason, but Mike McCarthy wants to see him out there this year.
The Steelers' new coach wants to see the four-time MVP on the field for the first two games of the preseason, and it just so happens that Pittsburgh will be facing two teams that Rodgers is very familiar with: The Green Bay Packers (Aug. 13) and the New York Jets (Aug. 21).
During a recent interview with The Athletic , Rodgers didn't sound thrilled at the idea of playing in the preseason, but he said he'll be out there if that's what McCarthy wants.
"He (wants me out there for) 30 or 40 plays," Rodgers said. "I said, 'Mike, if you want me to play, I'll play.' I'm not saying I want to do it. But if he wants me to, I will."
Preseason football isn't always must-see TV, but if Rodgers is on the field to face the Packers and the Jets, that will certainly add some intrigue to both games. The matchup against the Packers will be especially interesting with McCarthy also facing his old team. The Steelers coach spent 13 seasons in Green Bay before being fired in 2018. Back in 2010, Rodgers and McCarthy led the Packers to a Super Bowl win over the Steelers.
When McCarthy was hired as the Packers' head coach in 2006, it was pretty normal to have your starting QB play in the preseason, but over the past decade, it hasn't been as common.
Rodgers and McCarthy spent 13 seasons together in Green Bay, so the future Hall of Fame QB obviously knows McCarthy's offense well, but a few things have changed since they were last together back in 2018.
During his head-coaching stint in Dallas, McCarthy changed some of the lingo in his offense, and Rodgers is still trying to pick it up. Over the weekend, McCarthy sent in a play called "Snag Bo," which Rodgers loves, but he didn't even know what "Snag Bo" was when the call came in.
"It's one of my favorite plays going back to my rookie year -- basically a 'sit' route and a corner route -- that we always called 'Arrow,'" Rodgers told The Athletic. "I guess he calls it 'Snag' now. I've had to adjust a bit and be uncomfortable with some uncomfortable words."
That story from Rodgers is one reason training camp exists. You want to work out the kinks so there's no confusion when you get to Week 1. Of course, it's one thing to fix your mistakes in practice, and it's an entirely different thing to do it in a game. McCarthy clearly wants to ensure the offense is firing on all cylinders heading into the regular season, and the best way to do that is to have Rodgers and the unit on the field during the preseason.
If Rodgers does end up playing, it will be the most extensive preseason action he's seen in almost a decade. Rodgers saw a lot of action in 2018 during his final year with McCarthy in Green Bay, but in the seven seasons since, he's only played two preseason offensive series, both in 2023 with the Jets.
When it comes to letting your starting QB play in the preseason, every NFL coach seems to have a different philosophy. For instance, Sean McVay doesn't usually play his starters at all, and there's a zero % chance we'll see Matthew Stafford suit up in the preseason this year.
There are definitely a few reasons why playing your starters can be a bad idea, so let's take a look at why this might not be the best call for the Steelers.
1. Injuries happen and Rodgers is old. Yes, it's the preseason, but players still get injured all the time. If Aaron Rodgers is out on the field, he'll be facing off against defensive players who are trying to make the roster and the quickest way to do that is to rack up a quick sack on a soon-to-be Hall of Fame quarterback like Rodgers. The Bengals sent Joe Burrow out for some preseason action last year and he took a couple of big hits, including the one below in a game against the Commanders.
Probably don't want to see Joe Burrow doing this in a preseason game... Or in any game, for that matter. pic.twitter.com/0SgdPnU8TG
Hits like that can happen in the preseason, and if Rodgers were to get swallowed up like that, everyone in Pittsburgh would be holding their breath. QB injuries in the preseason are rare, but they do happen. The Jets lost Mark Sanchez to a season-ending injury in 2013 , and one year later, the Rams lost Sam Bradford to a preseason torn ACL . In 2016, Tony Romo injured his back in a preseason game , which set the stage for Dak Prescott to take over as the Cowboys' starting quarterback as a rookie.
Not only will there be an injury issue, but let's not forget that Rodgers is 42 years old. He's not as spry as he used to be and it's not as easy for him to escape defenders.
2. Steelers have a backup QB battle. The Steelers have one of the most intriguing backup QB battles in the NFL right now. They just used a third-round pick on Drew Allar, and he'll be competing with Mason Rudolph and 2025 sixth-round pick Will Howard for the right to back up Rodgers. It would certainly make sense to give these guys as many snaps as possible, but McCarthy obviously wants to see Rodgers get some game action, so the three backups likely won't see the field until the second quarter or later in the first two preseason games.
Putting your starters on the field in the preseason is always a risk, but the reward is that you feel like your team is better prepared for Week 1 and that's what McCarthy wants to see. With Rodgers headed into his final season, it will be almost fitting that his farewell tour begins in the preseason, with games against the only other teams he has ever played for.
author: John Breech

title: Aaron Rodgers credits wife Brittani for helping mend family rift after years of estrangement
summary: Rodgers said the reunion with his family has been a "couple-year process" and credited his wife's support
full_text:
As Aaron Rodgers prepares for what he insists is his final NFL season, he is also working on some elements of his personal life. It is well-known that the Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback is estranged from his family , but he recently posted photos with them on social media.
Rodgers captioned the series of photos, which included his parents, Darla and Ed Rodgers, and his older brother, Luke, "Another bonding week #fam."
After years of family division, Rodgers credited his wife, Brittani.
"Having those conversations with my wife – that allowed me to open up to the possibility of coming together," the four-time MVP said . "It's been a couple-year process now, the conversations with them. I've been very closed off about that part of my life, and I want to keep it that way, but there's been a narrative that's gone on for too long that I wanted to shut down and it's been really beautiful to reconnect with them, all of them."
The 42-year-old said Brittani never pressured him to reconcile, but was there during the journey of reuniting. He didn't say what initially caused the rift, citing that it is a private matter.
"I'm happy to be reunited," he said. "That part of my life is a really beautiful addition, and I gotta give my wife a lot of credit. Not that she was pushing me, because she never was, but just the way that she loves and supports me, having her by my side during this process was really special. I missed those relationships. And there was reasons for [the estrangement] that don't need to be talked about, but I'm thankful that that's come all the way back around."
The journey from estrangement to family photos on social media was not linear or quick. Rodgers called having each relationship in his life again a "blessing" and says he enjoyed spending time not only with his parents, but with his brother's "incredible" children as well, happy to "get to be an uncle."
The tension in the Rodgers family made headlines when the quarterback's younger brother, Jordan Rodgers, appeared on "The Bachelorette." The Rodgers family left two seats empty for Aaron and then-girlfriend Olivia Munn, who were not part of the family day of Jordan and the TV show's star JoJo Fletcher. In his 2024 documentary, Aaron expressed his anger towards that move, saying, "They go on a bullshit show and leave two empty chairs? They all agreed this was a good thing to do?"
Aaron was not present at Jordan and Fletcher's wedding. Other possible reasons for the rift include religion and Aaron's interest in plant medicine. Whatever caused the rift, Brittani was seemingly able to help her husband work through the difficulties.
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: Top 10 NFL head coaches entering 2026: Sean McVay clear No. 1, but NFC West foes closely behind
summary: CBS Sports' NFL experts ranked the league's best head coaches entering the 2026 season, with Sean McVay earning the top spot
full_text:
As the season rapidly approaches, CBS Sports' NFL experts ranked the top 10 head coaches leading teams into battle this year.
This exercise produced a wide variety of responses. Some coaches are offensive gurus; others are defensive geniuses. Still others don't specialize on one side or the other and are rather CEO-type leaders. Think Dan Campbell or the Harbaugh brothers, Jim and John. None of those three will call plays for either side of the ball this season, meaning their choices for who will handle those responsibilities are crucial.
Of course, just because they don't call plays doesn't mean they're not involved. The best coaches are intimately involved in every aspect. And that, of course, includes being a leader in and outside the locker room, designating roles and much, much more.
Each voter ranked their top 10 head coaches, and each spot was assigned a point value: 10 points for a first-place vote, nine for a second-place vote and one for a 10th-place vote.
Points: 108 | Highest rank: 1 | Lowest rank: 2
McVay, who sports a sterling 92-57 record (.617 win pct) and delivered winning seasons in eight of his nine years, has a near stranglehold on the top spot. Only two voters didn't have him first, and both had him second. McVay has been bold, pushing for the Matthew Stafford-for-Jared-Goff swap, even though he had been to a Super Bowl with Goff. It worked marvelously: Stafford and McVay won the Super Bowl in their first year together, and the two were on the doorstep of another trip last year.
McVay can clearly handle big-name superstars in the locker room, but his organization's grassroots talent recognition and development has also been crucial. There are so many mid- and late-round players who have turned into solid starters at the very least. Some, such as Puka Nacua , have become stars. McVay has also been adept at finding strong defensive coordinators: Raheem Morris, Wade Phillips, Brandon Staley and Chris Shula. On offense, his coaching tree includes current head coaches Liam Coen, Matt LaFleur, Mike LaFleur, Kevin O'Connell and Zac Taylor.
Simply put, there's a reason there's a Wikipedia page for the "Sean McVay effect." He has changed the game.
Points: 85 | Highest rank: 1 | Lowest rank: 6
Macdonald has been simply outstanding, and like McVay, he's done so while being bold. After a strong 10-7 debut season in Seattle, he was fine shipping Geno Smith off to the Raiders and firing offensive coordinator Ryan Grubb, simply because Macdonald had a different vision for his team. The Seahawks brought in Sam Darnold and Klint Kubiak and went on to win the Super Bowl. It's been impressive to see him transition to that aspect of head coaching responsibilities so easily.
It's no surprise that Macdonald has excelled defensively. He was an elite defensive coordinator in Baltimore before landing the top gig in Seattle, and he has absolutely flummoxed opponents at both stops. Last year, the Seahawks ranked first in scoring defense and sixth in total defense. Macdonald was terrific on the biggest stage, sending blitzers from all over against Drake Maye in the Super Bowl. Seattle's defense forced Maye into three turnovers and sacked him six times.
Macdonald's defensive designs, his knowledge of when to use them, and his ability to teach them to (and tailor them to) his players make him truly special.
Points: 84 | Highest rank: 2 | Lowest rank: 5
Shanahan's ability to get the most out of his quarterbacks is second to none. He went 38-17 and reached a Super Bowl with Jimmy Garoppolo , whose play outside the Bay Area has been lackluster. He is 30-15 with Brock Purdy as his starting quarterback, and when Purdy missed time last year, Mac Jones stepped in and went 5-3.
That adaptability seems to spread across the team, too. Shanahan's 49ers went 11-6 last year and won a playoff game despite just six players -- Christian McCaffrey , Kyle Juszczyk, Colton McKivitz , Dee Winters Kalia Davis and Deommodore Lenoir -- starting all 17 games. San Francisco was without George Kittle , Nick Bosa , Fred Warner , Purdy and many other top players for long stretches.
Of course, the elephant in the room is the Super Bowl. Shanahan has blown second-half leads in both Super Bowls he's been in with the 49ers, and he was the offensive coordinator for the Falcons ' infamous 28-3 collapse against the Patriots . If he doesn't ever lift a Lombardi Trophy, he will go down as one of the ultimate "so close yet so far" coaches, though at 46, one would think he has time.
Shanahan was at fault in a serious car accident this offseason and is on the mend, expecting to be available for Week 1.
Points: 80 | Highest rank: 2 | Lowest rank: 7
Reid came in eighth in CBS Sports' 20 best NFL coaches of all time , so how is he "only" fourth among the active coaches? Well, it's a "What have you done for me lately?" sort of business, and Reid is coming off a 6-11 season in which Patrick Mahomes and company looked simply ordinary. In truth, the offense has been just OK over the last three years, though Reid still has a Super Bowl title and a Super Bowl appearance during that span.
This will be a big year for Reid. The Chiefs are in a semi-reset after losing several top players, and Mahomes is on the mend from a torn ACL. Another down offensive year would be a tough look and lead to more questions. Overall, though, it's hard to question the three Lombardi Trophies, 279 wins and .640 winning percentage Reid has accrued.
Points: 58 | Highest rank: 3 | Lowest rank: 8
There is a steep drop-off here, and Payton is in fifth. But it's a pretty remarkable rise for Payton regardless. The offensive guru navigated the financially unprecedented release of Russell Wilson and took the Broncos to the playoffs each of the last two seasons anyway. Last year, they were likely a horribly unlucky Bo Nix ankle injury away from going to the Super Bowl.
Payton has a .630 career winning percentage and has won 13 or more games five times, including a career-high 14 last year. He is a brilliant offensive mind, though in an interesting twist, he is handing off play-calling duties to offensive coordinator Davis Webb . Expect Payton to still be heavily involved, though.
Points: 51 | Highest rank: 3 | Lowest rank: Unranked
Johnson exceeded even the highest of expectations last year, going 11-6 and winning a playoff game in his debut season. Johnson is the latest offensive whiz kid, but this somehow feels different, given Johnson's ability to win over the locker room and elevate what had been a downtrodden franchise.
Johnson, 40, proved his short but incredibly successful time as the Lions ' offensive coordinator was no fluke. He is excellent, especially in his blocking schemes. Guard Joe Thuney and center Drew Dalman were both Pro Bowlers last year, and guard Jonah Jackson and tackle Darnell Wright took huge steps forward. Caleb Williams had one of the league's lowest sack rates after struggling majorly in that facet as a rookie, and Chicago was among the best rushing attacks in the NFL.
Points: 38 | Highest rank: 3 | Lowest rank: Unranked
