Harbaugh's .679 career win percentage speaks for itself; it's a top-10 rate ever and second among active coaches behind only the Eagles ' Nick Sirianni. A former quarterback, Harbaugh is taking a big leap of faith this year after parting ways with longtime offensive coordinator/confidant Greg Roman and bringing in Mike McDaniel, who could not be in a starker juxtaposition. Harbaugh will also hope his newest defensive coordinator hire, Chris O'Leary, works out as well as his last one, Jesse Minter, did.
Points: 34 | Highest rank: 4 | Lowest rank: Unranked
Vrabel's value can be seen in how organizations perform when he's not there. Vrabel went 54-45 and made the postseason three times in six years with the Titans before being fired. The Titans are an NFL-worst 6-28 since. The Patriots went 4-13 in 2024, hired Vrabel and went 14-3 and made the Super Bowl last year. Numbers don't lie. Vrabel's…
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Highest-paid players at every NFL position: A look at who is cashing the biggest check heading into 2026
summary: A look at the markets by position for 2026
full_text:
The NFL offseason is almost over, and we've already seen some big moves and changes. Free agency and the NFL Draft are behind us, and with training camp approaching, we can practically smell the pigskin and taste the tailgate food that soon awaits.
It's no secret that the NFL is a money-making machine: from merchandise, to commercials, streaming services to tickets and more. Money is often a big hurdle between teams and players, with contract holdouts, hold-ins and trades giving each season plenty of drama on the sidelines.
The NFL salary cap has more than doubled in the last decade-plus and now sits at over $300 million per team heading into 2026. Some teams are known to be more willing to spend money, while others like to be more cautious with the paycheck.
Some players decide to take less to be on the team they want, or to regain a solid core around them, while others demand the highest value at their position. Just who are the ones taking home the biggest bag?
We broke down the highest-paid players by position, based on average annual value, to get a feel for where the market stands. All values are via Spotrac .
Patrick Mahomes agreed this offseason to terms on a revised contract that adds two years to his existing deal and makes him the highest-paid quarterback in average annual value. The three-time Super Bowl MVP and two-time NFL MVP is the first player in NFL history to sign a contract worth more than $500 million. He passed Dak Prescott , who previously held the title at $60 million per year. Followed by Mahomes and Prescott are Josh Allen , Joe Burrow , Trevor Lawrence , Jordan Love and Matthew Stafford , who all hold $55 million AAV deals, according to Spotrac.
Saquon Barkley earned his payday after a historic 2024 season, where he not only earned NFL Offensive Player of the Year, an All-Pro honor and was the rushing leader, but he also took home a Super Bowl ring. Barkley was pivotal in the Super Bowl run, setting the league record for most rushing yards in a single season (2,504), including playoffs.
The 32-year-old went undrafted in 2017 before signing with the Baltimore Ravens . He signed with the Giants this offseason after earning Pro Bowl and second-team All-Pro honors in 2025.
Jaxon Smith-Njigba was essential in the Seahawks ' Super Bowl champion run last season, as the NFL's Offensive Player of the Year. He had 119 receptions and 1,793 receiving yards, a league high, along with 10 touchdowns in the regular season. His breakout year came at the perfect time for Sam Darnold's offense and he has high expectations as he enters Year 4.
George Kittle is arguably the best tight end in the league right now and it shows in his contract. The seven-time Pro Bowler and two-time first-team All-Pro has spent his entire career with the 49ers . Kittle started and ended his season with injuries last year, missing five games due to a hamstring tear suffered in Week 1 and going down with an Achilles injury in their wild card game against the Eagles . He still has goals of a Week 1 return for the 2026 season.
Laremy Tunsil was the No. 13 overall pick in 2016, selected by the Miami Dolphins . He then went to the Houston Texans before joining the Commanders in 2025. His resume includes five Pro Bowl honors and he has started all 139 games he's played in.
Tyler Smith beats out last year's highest-paid offensive guard Trey Smith , who earns an average of $23.5 million per year. The 2022 No. 24 overall pick has become pivotal on the Cowboys ' line and has three Pro Bowls during his time in the league.
Tyler Linderbaum was drafted No. 25 overall in 2022 by the Ravens, where he remained until this offseason when he joined the Raiders . The three-time Pro Bowler took 99% of offensive snaps last season, starting all 17 games.
Will Anderson Jr . became the highest-paid non-quarterback in NFL history with his massive three-year, $150 million deal. According to Next Gen Stats, he was seventh in run-stop rate (12.6%), third in run stuffs (13) and second in pressures (85) among defenders with at least 150 run defensive snaps in 2025. His performance put him second in NFL Defensive Player of the Year voting. He was named DPOY in 2023.
Jeffery Simmons briefly held the title of highest-paid interior defensive lineman this offseason before Jalen Carter took the throne with a huge extension on the eve of the first practice of training camp. Carter's extension doesn't kick in until after the 2027 season and includes $106 million guaranteed.
Fred Warner has spent his entire career with the Niners and the team has him under contract until 2030. He is a four-time first-team All-Pro and a four-time Pro Bowler, starting all 121 regular-season and 12 playoff games he's appeared in. The defensive leader was limited to six games last season due to an ankle fracture.
For the second time in his career, Ward tops the highest-paid defensive back list after signing a two-year, $62.2 million extension that ties him to Cleveland through 2029. Ward was already signed through 2027 on a five-year, $100.5 million extension in 2022. He's a five-time Pro Bowler with 18 career interceptions.
Derwin James has played for the Chargers since the team selected him No. 17 overall in 2018. He earned his fifth Pro Bowl and fourth second-team All-Pro honor last season. He had a career-best three interceptions last season, to go with 94 combined tackles, seven passes defended, two sacks and one forced fumble.
This marks the largest deal for a kicker in league history, earned in thanks to Pro Bowls in each of his three seasons in the NFL. Aubrey went undrafted in 2022 and joined the USFL, becoming a two-time champion in the league, before heading to the Cowboys in 2023. He has made 88.2% of field goals attempted and 96.9% of attempted extra points. He has six total field goals over 60 yards, an NFL record.
Jordan Stout led the league with a net average of 44.9 yards last season and earned a Pro Bowl spot due to his 2025 performance.

full_text:

title: NFL training camp QB battles: Breaking down four competitions, plus veterans that need to watch their backs
summary: Training camp has brought several quarterback competitions into focus, with Week 1 roles still unsettled around the league
full_text:
When it comes to training camp storylines, quarterback battles take center stage. This summer, we have a handful of battles to sink our teeth into, ranging from Atlanta, Minnesota, Cleveland and Las Vegas. On top of those battles, there are also a few signal callers in precarious positions. Their jobs are necessarily at risk, but they have plenty to prove to put themselves on a stronger footing.
Below, we take the temperature of the four quarterback battles currently underway, highlighting the latest updates from camp, plus give our prediction of who we see coming out on top. Then, we'll put the spotlight on a handful of veteran quarterbacks who aren't in a battle, but need to watch their backs.
Kyler Murray and J.J. McCarthy are entrenched in a head-to-head competition for the Week 1 job in Minnesota. To begin camp, Kevin O'Connell split the reps between the two signal-callers, but Murray does appear to be gaining momentum as of late. Murray showcased his best practice of camp on Saturday, according to a wide array of reports at Vikings camp, including ESPN's Kevin Seifert . Most importantly, he was on the field for 16 of the first team offense's 22 snaps on 11-on-11 drills, per Seifert. He also completed all three of his passes to Justin Jefferson during the session, which is a key rapport metric to monitor. As for McCarthy, who did get more snaps over Murray during Friday's session (32 vs. 26 in full-offense drills), didn't have as successful a practice on Saturday as Murray.
While that's the up-close view of this battle, at a more macro level, it's hard not to see Murray coming out on top. McCarthy is coming off a 2025 season, his first as the full-time starter, where he struggled mightily. He went 6-4 over his 10 starts and completed 57.6% of his passes, averaged 163.2 passing yards per game, and registered 11 touchdowns with 12 interceptions. His 72.6 passer rating ranked last among qualified quarterbacks. While McCarthy did seem to find his footing down the stretch (4-0 record with a 100.4 passer rating), that didn't stop Minnesota from signing Murray as a free agent. While Murray has a shaky injury history (has missed 30 of a possible 68 games over the last five seasons), his talent provides a much higher upside for O'Connell's offense.
Prediction : Kyler Murray wins the Week 1 job.
The Falcons technically have a quarterback battle on their hands between Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr,, but it hasn't exactly been a slugfest. Why? Well, injuries have gotten in the way of this being a true competition. Of course, the most notable injury surrounds Penix, who is still rehabbing from a torn ACL he suffered in Week 11 last season. New coach Kevin Stefanski said last week that Penix is still not cleared for full team activities , which means he cannot take part in 11-on-11 drills. Penix also provided an update to reporters, and the timeline isn't encouraging for his chances to secure the Week 1 gig. He noted that it could be another four weeks before reaching the next stage of his rehabilitation. If you tack that into the calendar, Penix is looking at being cleared by the end of August, meaning he'd likely miss all of the preseason. Under that scenario, it's hard to imagine him truly pushing Tagovailoa.
Speaking of Tagovailoa, he also was not on the field last week due to a reported back injury. Stefanski described the injury as minor and the former Dolphins quarterback "will be out there sooner rather than later." Under different circumstances with a healthy Penix, this could've been a pocket for Tagovailoa to lose some ground. Instead, it won't really move the needle.
Prediction : Tua Tagovailoa wins the Week 1 job.
In Cleveland, first-year coach Todd Monken is mulling whether to name Deshaun Watson or Shedeur Sanders the starter for the Browns in 2026. Through the early days of camp, it doesn't appear as though either quarterback has truly endeared himself. Watson has thrown multiple interceptions in two of the four practice days, according to The Athletic . Despite that, Monken tipped his hand in favor of Sanders, continuing to split the reps between the two with the first-team offense.
As a rookie, Sanders went 3-4 for the Browns, and the passing metrics leave little to be desired. For the season, he completed 57% of his passes, threw seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions, and posted a 68.1 passer rating. Since his debut in Week 11, Sanders threw an NFL-high 10 picks. That said, Sanders has noted this summer that he feels much more comfortable heading into his second season, so that could help level out those numbers amid this battle with Watson.
As for Watson, he hasn't played since tearing his Achilles in Week 7 of the 2024 season. He also suffered another tear in that same Achilles tendon during his rehab, which resulted in him missing the entire 2025 season. In all, he's played in just 19 games over the last four seasons since coming over to the Browns in that blockbuster trade with the Texans . While he's shown plenty of rust over the course of camp thus far, it does seem like Monken is giving him the space to shake it off and, at times, feels like he has the inside track at the job.
Prediction : Deshaun Watson wins the Week 1 job.
As we look to Las Vegas, it's less of a quarterback competition and more of a philosophical approach with how the Raiders want to handle the development of Fernando Mendoza , who they selected with the No. 1 overall pick at the 2026 NFL Draft . Klint Kubiak has stated that he believes the best way to usher a young quarterback into the NFL is to bring him along slowly and not start him in the game. The ideal approach is to have an established veteran begin the year and then eventually hand the keys over to him when he's ready.
The Raiders have an established veteran on the roster in Kirk Cousins , and he's been the top quarterback throughout the offseason. That includes Kubiak putting Cousins out there as QB1 on the first day of training camp to work with the first-team offense. Even if Mendoza takes training camp by storm, Kubiak's path for the young quarterback could lead to him starting his career as Cousins' backup. That said, it's only a matter of time before the Mendoza era begins in Sin City.
Prediction : Kirk Cousins wins the Week 1 job.
Mayfield isn't in danger of losing his starting job, but his future with the Buccaneers beyond 2026 is murky at best. The veteran enters the final year of his contract and, after the two sides were unable to come to terms on an extension by his self-imposed deadline, negotiations are over. Now, Mayfield is focusing on the upcoming season, which could very well be his last in Tampa, especially after he acknowledged publicly that he felt "disrespected" by the organization.
This adds another layer of pressure for Mayfield, who is looking to rebound after his worst statistical season since becoming the Bucs starter. The 31-year-old is not only now tasked with bringing the Buccaneers back to the playoffs after an 8-9 campaign in 2025 snapped their streak of five-straight postseason appearances, but he's also again forced to prove his worth for a new contract (either with the Bucs or some other team as he eyes free agency in 2027).
After sitting out for the bulk of the offseason program as he sought a revised contract, the Cardinals agreed on a reworked deal with Brissett that will pay him up to $21 million in 2026, including $15.5 million guaranteed. While Brissett got his desired contract, it doesn't guarantee that he'll start the entire season for Arizona. The veteran will almost certainly be the Cardinals' QB1 to begin the 2026 campaign, but the franchise does have rookie Carson Beck waiting in the wings. The club selected the Miami quarterback in the third round of the draft this offseason, and will likely want to see what they have in him at some point. That's especially true if the season goes awry and they are in line for a top pick at the 2027 NFL Draft. Before…
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: Can Patriots repeat? Drake Maye, Mike Vrabel face tougher 2026 road after stunning Super Bowl run
summary: After one of the greatest turnarounds in NFL history, the Patriots enter 2026 with higher expectations, a tougher schedule and major questions to answer
full_text:
The New England Patriots turned the tide in 2025. After three straight seasons of under .500 ball and two consecutive 4-13 campaigns, the Patriots catapulted into Super Bowl contention. With Drake Maye entering his second season and under new coach Mike Vrabel, the organization went 14-3 in the regular season and advanced to Super Bowl LX. While they were unable to hoist the Lombardi Trophy, falling to the Seattle Seahawks , it was still a historic turnaround for the franchise.
In fact, their 17-4 record (including playoffs) is the largest year-over-year win increase in NFL history (+13). They were also the first team ever to reach the Super Bowl following a 13-plus loss season. Helping spearhead that resurrection, Vrabel won Coach of the Year, while Maye finished second in MVP voting.
That Super Bowl run a season ago has not only put the Patriots back on the map but also raised the bar for what the region and the NFL expected of them heading into 2026. Labeled as one of the true contenders throughout the league, they won't catch teams sleeping as they may have in 2025, and the road ahead is far more treacherous.
Below, we'll comb through New England's upcoming schedule in 2026, highlight their key offseason additions and departures, and also highlight what they'll need to overcome to continue this ascent.
vs. Detroit Lions (Munich)
On paper, the 2026 Patriots are much more talented than the 2025 Patriots. They added some major weapons like A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs , bolstered the offensive line, and added some key pieces to the defense as well. While this version of New England may be better than last year's, its record may not be.
One of the biggest critiques of the Patriots from 2025 was that they stacked up a ton of wins because of an easy schedule. In the regular season, New England had the easiest strength of schedule since the 1999 Rams . As we look forward to this coming season, the road will not be as kind.
From the jump, the Patriots will be tested to a historic degree. They have the hardest strength of schedule from Week 1 through Week 4 (.721 opponent win percentage in 2025) in the last 40 years (1986 Eagles ). Three of those four games also take place on the road, adding another layer of difficulty. They are the first team since the 2019 Dolphins to open the season with three straight division winners. For reference, New England faced two division winners all of last season.
Beyond that grueling first month, New England enters the season with the sixth-hardest strength of schedule overall, and the AFC should be much more competitive this time around. Joe Burrow missed a chunk of the season due to injury, eliminating the Bengals as a contender, while Lamar Jackson and the Ravens and Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs also experienced down years. Provided those quarterbacks stay healthy, they should be among the top rivals to New England as they jockey for playoff positioning, along with their division rival in the Buffalo Bills.
So, if the Patriots succeed anywhere close to the level they reached in 2025, detractors won't have the easy-schedule narrative to lean on.
via DraftKings Sportsbook.
Currently, the biggest story surrounding the Patriots as they go through the initial days of training camp is that All-Pro cornerback Christian Gonzalez is still without a contract extension.
Earlier in camp, owner Robert Kraft told a group of reporters in Foxborough that the team had offered a contract that would make Gonzalez, who is under team control through 2027 (fifth-year option), the highest-paid corner in the NFL and the highest-paid player in franchise history. Despite that, pen has not been put to paper on a new deal. Unlike Kraft, Gonzalez chose not to discuss the negotiations publicly when asked about them at camp.
This is puzzling on a couple of different fronts. When it comes to Kraft saying they've offered him a market-setting extension, there might be some nuance there. The two sides aren't close to an agreement at the moment, Albert Breer of the MMQB told NBC Sports Boston just a few days ago. So, while an offer may have been extended to Gonzalez, it may not be to the caliber of the corner's liking, especially with the Seattle Seahawks and fellow defensive back Devon Witherspoon also narrowing in on a market-altering extension. Maybe Gonzalez and company are waiting for that deal to go down in hopes of boosting his value even higher?
Gonzalez has been taking part in New England's offseason program and has been on the field throughout training camp, neglecting to enact a hold-in, as many other players seeking a new contract do nowadays. In fact, he's basically done the opposite. Gonzalez was on the field as a full participant during the team's first day of padded practices, which was eye-opening. Typically, players would draw the line at participating in full-padded practices to avoid an injury becoming a sticking point in negotiations, but Gonzalez is going through the workouts in good faith.
Even though it hasn't become a speed bump in terms of the Patriots' on-field preparations for the 2026 season, getting Gonzalez done sooner rather than later is paramount.
Drake Maye was walloped in the playoffs. Throughout the postseason, Maye was sacked 21 times, which is the most in a single playoff run all-time. That constant pressure led to the MVP runner-up struggling mightily, and it all came to a head in Super Bowl LX, where Maye became the first player with three-plus turnovers in the second half of a Super Bowl since Rich Gannon in 2002. A key reason for Maye being under so much duress was poor play along the offensive line, particularly at left tackle with then-rookie Will Campbell .
Despite his struggles, the Patriots are sticking with their former No. 4 overall pick at left tackle. That said, the franchise did put resources towards bolstering the line this offseason. In free agency, they added Alijah Vera-Tucker by inking him to a three-year, $42 million contract. He'll slot in at left guard, and Jared Wilson will kick in to his natural center position after trading Garrett Bradbury to the Chicago Bears.
New England still has Morgan Moses at right tackle and Mike Onwenu at right guard, but did use the 28th overall pick at the 2026 NFL Draft to bring in tackle Caleb Lomu . The 6-foot-6, 313-pounder played left tackle at Utah, so he could be a failsafe option if Campbell's struggles continue. That said, he's been eyed by the team as the future at right tackle, given that Moses is entering his age-35 season.
Outside of getting Gonzalez's extension done, the biggest concern for the Patriots defense is the lack of top-tier talent and depth off the edge. This offseason, New England saw edge rusher K'Lavon Chaisson sign with the Commanders . Chaisson was second on the team with 7.5 sacks over the regular season, and was tied for the team lead in sacks over the playoffs (3).
Meanwhile, Harold Landry , who led the team in sacks last season, has opened camp on the PUP list as he continues to deal with a knee injury he suffered last season.
The team did add to the position group, signing veteran Dre'Mont Jones to a three-year, $39.5 million contract in free agency. Between the Ravens and Titans last season, Jones had seven total sacks and 24 quarterback hits, which were both career highs. They also drafted Gabe Jacas in the second round out of Illinois, but the pass rusher was just recently activated off the non-football injury list following a cleanup procedure on his knee after the draft.
With Landry's availability in question, New England is counting on Jones and/or Jacas to contribute in a big way out of the gate.
The most scandalous story surrounding the Patriots' offseason centered around their head coach, Mike Vrabel. The 2026 Coach of the Year was photographed at a Sedona resort with former NFL reporter for The Athletic, Dianna Russini. The two, who are married to different people, were pictured in a hot tub together and interlocking…

title: Former No. 1 pick Jadeveon Clowney heading back to Texans for second stint: 'It was a no-brainer for me'
summary: Clowney is back with the Texans after closing last season with a career-best three-sack game
full_text:
It's never too late to come home, something three-time Pro Bowl edge rusher Jadeveon Clowney just found out.
The 2014 NFL Draft's first overall pick is returning to the Houston Texans after agreeing to terms on a contract, according to ESPN . Clowney concluded his 2025 season with the Dallas Cowboys with a bang, racking up a single-game career-high three sacks in Week 18 against New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart . Despite not suiting up for the Cowboys until Week 4, he finished with 8.5 sacks, his most in a season since producing 9.5 in 2023 with the Ravens . That figure also led Dallas in 2025.
"It's great," Clowney said in a phone interview with KPRC 2 in Houston . "It was a family decision. It wasn't about the money it was about chasing my legacy and chasing a Super bowl . I've got a lot of game left and want to contribute."
Now, there's a chance the former first-overall pick could play even better in 2026 at 33-years-old after going through training camp with the Texans alongside Houston's All-Pro edge rusher duo of Will Anderson Jr . and Danielle Hunter .
Anderson's 12 sacks tied for the eighth-most in the league in 2025 while ranking third in the NFL in quarterback pressures with 93. Anderson's 21% quarterback pressure rate led the league in 2025 among those with at least 300 pass rushes, per CBS Sports Research. That all added up to Anderson's first first-team All-Pro selection in his three-season career, in addition to being extended on a three-year, $150 million deal this offseason. His $50 million average per year salary makes him the highest-paid non-quarterback in the league. Hunter's 15.0 sacks in 2025 ranked as the third-most in the NFL, while his 83 quarterback pressures stood as the fifth-most in the NFL last season. The duo of Anderson Jr. and Hunter has produced 50.0 sacks combined since 2024, the most in the NFL.
"I was excited about paying with those guys, too," Clowney said. "Good defense, and I can help contribute and good chance to chase a Super Bowl. I know what it looks like I can help this squad."
Clowney enters the 2026 season with 66.5 career sacks, 120 tackles for loss, 16 forced fumbles and 15 fumble recoveries. His three fumble returns for scores rank as the most in the league among active players. The NFL's No. 1 total defense (277.2 total yards per game allowed in 2025) and No. 2 scoring defense (17.4 points per game allowed in 2025) is now a little richer following the addition of Clowney at the early onset of training camp.
"For sure, I was so excited. I had more opportunities. When I found out the Texans were interested, it was a no-brainer for me," Clowney said, via KPRC 2 in Houston . "It was comfortable for me to do that. I was excited to help the situation."

He also worked out for the Cleveland Browns recently. However, […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TX - DECEMBER 21: Jadeveon Clowney #42 of the Dallas Cowboys rushes the passer during an NFL football game against the Los Angeles Chargers at AT&T Stadium on December 21, 2025 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Arizona Cardinals may – or may not – need another pass rusher opposite EDGE rusher Josh Sweat. Looking at the free agent list of available pass rushers, Jadeveon Clowney remained unsigned. There was a recent buzz about Clowney going to an NFC West club. He also worked out for the Cleveland Browns recently. However, Clowney signed with the Houston Texans. RELATED: COULD CLOWNEY BE COMING TO THE CARDINALS? Clowney, age 33, was drafted by Houston back in 2014 as the first overall pick. He played for the Texans for five seasons. And now, he is going back to the team that brought him into the league. It has been mentioned that the Cardinals might need another pass rusher. Darius Robinson was taken in the first round a few years ago to become the pass rusher on that left side. Zaven Collins has become the main guy on that side with Baron Browning as his backup. Both players have been given a good number of snaps. Is this enough? Are these players taking care of the opposite side’s pass rush? Clowney was looked at as a possible answer and was available. He had a bit of a resurgence as a pass rusher, which would have helped. Clowney has compiled 24.5 sacks in the past three seasons. He signed a one-year deal with Houston. Exact financial terms of the contract were not immediately disclosed. He lives in Houston in the offseason, so it makes sense. During Clowney’s five seasons with the Texans, he was a three-time Pro Bowler and earned a second-team All-Pro nod. After leaving Houston after the 2018 season, he has played with six other NFL clubs, including the Dallas Cowboys last year. Clowney has 66.5 career sacks with career earnings of $100,507,718.

title: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur’s Sunday press conference
summary: Arizona Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur waited for his team’s Sunday training camp session to be completed before he dove into a scheduled press conference with the media. There were quite a few issues and topics to be discussed. The coach seems to be anxious to get this year’s schedule on the road, including playing […]
full_text: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Arizona Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur waited for his team’s Sunday training camp session to be completed before he dove into a scheduled press conference with the media. There were quite a few issues and topics to be discussed. The coach seems to be anxious to get this year’s schedule on the road, including playing in the annual Hall of Fame Game on this Thursday, August 6. RELATED: CARDINALS FIRST 2026 OFFICIAL DEPTH CHART Here is what LaFleur said at the presser: —————————————————————————— Q: Have you encountered any scorpions since you arrived? LaFleur: It’s so funny you ask that. Yeah, about two weeks ago, my wife was going down and tucked in the kids, and there was a nice-sized scorpion right outside the little man’s room. So, that was our first encounter. Needless to say, there were people at the house the next day spraying. Q: What do you got on injuries right now in terms of guys that are healthy, limping off the field, that kind of stuff? LaFleur: Walt’s (Nolen) good. More of sometimes you name the player when they’ve had a serious injury like they did. It’s a process both mentally and physically getting through that. So, he’s good. Which is obviously a good thing for most importantly him, but the Cardinals as well. And then we’re going to hold Joey (Blount) out today. He got a stinger. What you guys know about his past injuries and stuff from the neck up, we’re going to do some more testing and go from there. Q: Was it anything that Walt felt? LaFleur: Just a little discomfort. He was not comfortable in that knee. He had an issue with a year ago. So, we checked it all out. Everything looked good and he’ll be ready to roll today. We look at that defensive line. Q: The depth that you guys kind of collected, how are you seeing it right now? How crucial are guys like Nolan and Darius (Robinson) to take that step? LaFleur: Not just those two. Like you said, the entire depth. I’ve been on a very good football team that didn’t have a very good defensive line, but it wreaked havoc. We’ve talked about in here about the quarterback being the most important position in sports, and it’s about as hard as it gets. But I’ll tell you what, that D-line, they got to cause havoc up there, snap in and snap out. The importance of having depth so those guys can, when they’re out there, they can go, and then you can send in that kind of next platoon. I won’t even call them the twos, just the next platoon to get after, whether it be in the run game, setting edges, attacking, making it difficult for the offensive line, or obviously, rushing the passer there on third down. So, haven’t totally had that conversation in front of the team yet in terms of what I think of the D-line and O-line, for that matter. But this D-line needs to go, and they need to go hard. Q: Besides obviously getting more reps for your players, more teaching time for your coaches, what’s the big advantage of playing in this game a week before everybody? LaFleur: Yeah, I think you just said it. I’ve been on record just how excited I was to get that one extra block, right? And having that extra game. But then, if we have to kind of maneuver a day, we built so many reps off of that first block. So, just the totality of what that’s going to provide for us. And then you think about the game. I’m going to hold off. I don’t know if anyone’s going to ask me. I’m going to hold off in terms of saying who’s going to play. And I’ll tell you why. Mainly, I want these guys only focused on now. Like it’s the preseason – those games matter in the moment. But what really matters in the preseason is the practice that we’re preparing for. And that’s where I want these guys, and that’s where I know those guys are at. So, the guys that do play, it’s their first time out there where coaches aren’t right behind them or giving them a script. There is no script. We’ll be tight with our plan. I want to see is these guys – their play style come to life, and us go operate before the snap. That’s it. And then everything else is those guys going out and letting it loose. Q: That said, what’s your plan for this week as you as you go through the week here? LaFleur: Yep. So, the same block. We got our practice today coming off an off day, which typically is going to be just a tick less of reps from what you guys saw in these last two practices. Tomorrow will be fun. Really fun in terms of just the amount of reps, and there’ll be some really good work put in. Then we’ll go back to our jog-through day and then our travel day. Which will resemble the third practice of that four-day block. We will be practicing, and we’ll be getting after it that morning. We just have to modify in terms of the guys that are playing, the guys that aren’t playing, and obviously the travel time from the Phoenix airport to take off to Cleveland. Q: Jeremiyah stood up here the other day and insisted he wanted and needed to play in this game. Do you take any players’ input on whether they want to play, or is it your plan and you just need to tell them whatever the plan is? LaFleur: It’ll never just be my plan. It’s going to be a collective and communicative effort in terms of great communication amongst everybody to see who needs it and who doesn’t. For instance, name a player that’s been in a league for 10-plus years that’s played a lot of football. It’s probably going to be a little different than a rookie, right? I appreciate Jeremiah saying that. I know these guys love football. They want to play. I learned really early in this league it’s the preseason. It doesn’t matter in terms of the win-loss, but these guys are still out there fighting for jobs, too. Trying to put their best product out there, and they’re putting their bodies on the line like it’s real football, and if the guys that are playing, if they don’t go out with that mindset, I mean, that’s how you get hurt. It’s how you don’t put a good product on the field. I kind of almost made the mistake in my mind as a coach when I first got into it about just probably not being as serious as I needed to be with the players, and I learned really quickly. So, we’ll have the guys that are playing. It’s an amped-up environment. It’s real. Q: You talked about your plan leading up to the game on Thursday. What’s your plan after the game when you guys can get back to it with practice? Is anyone sticking around for the ceremony on Saturday? What does that look like? LaFleur: I follow one block at a time. So, not honestly, I’m not even there yet in terms of what’s today? Sunday. Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday. We play Thursday. I don’t even get home until four in the morning, whatever it is, three in the morning. We got to evaluate the film, and then we got to get ready for that next block. When Larry (Fitzgerald) gets inducted, and he gets his speech and his time there, that’s going to be a pretty special moment. But I am really not even there yet with that next block. I just know that when that next block comes, we still have a four-day deal, which is great. That fourth day is going to coincide with us taking off from here and getting back to Tempe, and that’ll be uh two days before we play Vegas. That’s really all I know so far. With preseason being such a different idea for rookies, having not played preseason games in college. Do you talk to them at all as a group saying, “Hey, like this is how you should approach the scheme,” or is that anything differently than how you I don’t want to over-talk it. It’s just a game, and again, when you put your body on the line, and it’s real live bullets out there, you’ve got to mentally get yourself right. That’s not a problem as long as we approach it that way. And so, we won’t over-talk about it. It’s just, hey, we got to go play good football. We got to operate the right way, and our play styles got to come to life. And then when the ball snaps, you got to go execute. And sometimes…

full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - FEBRUARY 08: WR Stefon Diggs (8) of the New England Patriots looks on holding his helmet during the Seattle Seahawks versus the New England Patriots Super Bowl LX game on February 8, 2026, at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, CA. (Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images We’re several days into training camp, and closer to the season. One’s mind can’t help but drift toward what this team will look like in September, after the cutdown deadline and what we hope is a healthy, productive August. With the team still shaky on depth at a handful of positions—we are nervously looking at you, right tackle—could they make an unexpected veteran addition? Or is there an expected contributor who might get the axe at a deep spot? Tre’Shon Diaz, Saivion Mixson, and Dave Choate give their takes. We’re then looking for yours, as always. Add: Stefon Diggs The Athletic’s Daniel Popper ruined the surprise a bit, but I still believe, with everything surrounding James Pearce, Jr., picking up Stefon Diggs would be a shock to the majority of Falcons fans. But I can’t rule it out. Diggs, at this stage of his career, does give either Penix or Tagovailoa a security blanket on passing downs, not to mention another veteran that can help maximize Zachariah Branch’s ability in space. The allegations and bad press may have knocked his price tag down to a point where Kevin Stefanski, who worked with Diggs for five seasons, could pull the trigger. —Saivion Mixson Cut: Cameron Thomas While Thomas was just signed this offseason, his contract is structured in a way that doesn’t indicate he has a guaranteed spot. Last season, the team made a similar deal with DE Morgan Fox, who became a surprise cut himself, and I could see the same happening to Thomas. The Falcons DE/EDGE room is crowded; the team has formed a competitive room with a mix of young and veteran talent, and Thomas’s path to play time is already hampered by his lack of pass rush ability. If James Pearce Jr. is able to start the season without a suspension, then I could see Thomas being the odd man out by the end of camp. — Tre’Shon Diaz Add: Jack Conklin The pieces fit together pretty neatly here. The Falcons currently have a tackle problem, in that both Jawaan Taylor and Wanya Morris are dealing with injuries, and everyone behind them is fairly inexperienced. This is a team that may want more insurance heading into the season. Conklin is not renowned for his durability, either, but he spent four years as a starting tackle with Bill Callahan in Cleveland and was a quality right tackle during that stretch. The Browns cut ties with him this offseason and he has yet to find a home, but joining an Atlanta team with Callahan and a lot of uncertainty at tackle makes a lot of sense if another team isn’t willing to give him a clear-cut starting job. I suspect no team will. — Dave Choate

title: Falcons legend Todd McClure joins franchise’s front office
summary: For more than a decade, Todd McClure paved the way for running backs and protected quarterbacks in Atlanta, with fellow franchise icons like Warrick Dunn, Michael Turner, Michael Vick, and Matt Ryan benefiting from his skill. Now, McClure will once again try to give Falcons players what they need to thrive, but in an entirely […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GA - OCTOBER 30: Former offensive lineman Todd McClure of the Atlanta Falcons, left, talks with owner Arthur Blank of the Atlanta Falcons before a game against the Carolina Panthers at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 30, 2022 in Atlanta, Georgia. McClure was inducted into the 2022 Atlanta Falcons Ring of Honor at halftime. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images For more than a decade, Todd McClure paved the way for running backs and protected quarterbacks in Atlanta, with fellow franchise icons like Warrick Dunn, Michael Turner, Michael Vick, and Matt Ryan benefiting from his skill. Now, McClure will once again try to give Falcons players what they need to thrive, but in an entirely different role. McClure is one of several hires announced by the Falcons on Monday, joining Atlanta’s front office as the new coordinator of player development and a senior personnel assistant. The Ring of Honor inductee, who previously held the team’s record for consecutive starts, is one of the best centers in history alongside legends like Jeff Van Note and Alex Mack and has remained an outspoken champion for and fan of the Falcons into his retirement. A seventh round pick in 1999, McClure overcame a major injury that wiped out his rookie season and became a key cog on some terrific offensive lines all the way until his retirement in 2013. Like Matt Ryan, McClure is not coming into this role with a wealth of experience, but he is joining up with extensive football experience, the full trust of the franchise, and likely a glowing endorsement from Ryan. McClure has been around the Falcons for a long time now and was credited as a leader and player instrumental to Ryan’s growth during his playing career. Per the team, “ McClure will support the club’s player development program by coordinating cross-functional initiatives and assisting football leadership with player-focused and strategic projects .” We’ll see what that actually translates to in practice—it’s likely a role McClure will learn as he goes, much like Ryan is learning his president of football role—but at a minimum it is very fun to have Mud Duck back in the building. No one should be surprised if former Falcons from the most successful era in franchise history continue to join up in some capacity, as the team is trying hard to bring back both the memory of better days and actual better days. The rationale is that players who made the team thrive can do the same thing in different roles, and while we don’t yet know how that’s going to work out, it does feel a bit more promising than the past eight years of mediocre football and oft-combative stances with their own fanbase that the Falcons are trying to put behind them. McClure brings the right kind of enthusiasm and a wealth of playing experience to this, after all. The team also announced several other new hires without the same level of name recognition. National scout Justin Hickman played in both the CFL and NFL before moving into scouting, and spent the past few years working for the Patriots as an area scout. This is a promotion for him and was originally reported back in April , but the team is now making it official. During his tenure in New England, the team added players from the Midwest region Hickman worked in like Ohio State’s TreyVeon Henderson, Eastern Michigan’s Sidy Sow, and former Falcon Sam Roberts. BLESTO scout Daniel Clements is making the leap from college, where he spent the past few seasons with Texas and Texas A&M as in personnel roles. In those roles, he had significant evaluation experience for high school and college prospects, and will join the Falcons and the BLESTO scouting cooperative hoping to turn that experience into gold for Atlanta. Area scout Keith Earle is an Ian Cunningham hire through-and-through. He’s worked with Cunningham both as an area scout with the Bears and as a player personnel intern with the Eagles, overlapping with the Falcons’ general manager, and is clearly someone Cunningham has a lot of trust in. Area scout Kevin Melore is getting a promotion after spending 2025 as a scouting assistant for Atlanta. Prior to that, he worked in scouting with Texas (the college, not the state). Scouting assistant Max Blank steps into Melore’s old role, or at least one with an identical title, and as you would guess is Arthur Blank’s son. He’s had two scouting internships with the Falcons, one with the Rams, and worked in a “rotational analyst” role the team describes as “focused on player engagement, growth audiences and player personnel.” Blank will continue climbing the scouting ladder with a team he’s extremely familiar with. Finally, assistant director of scouting and conditioning Frank Wintrich has a pretty rich background in his role. Wintrich has been the director of health and fitness at the National Defense University, a human performance manager at the Department of Justice, and prior to those roles piled up nearly two decades in strength and conditioning and football performance roles across college football. Give the new hires a warm welcome, if you would.

title: Falcons training camp Day 5 news, standouts, interviews, injuries
summary: The Falcons returned to the practice field on Monday after a day off on Sunday, and delivered arguably the best practice of training camp so far. With the pads on for the first time, energy was high and we got the longest practice session—which inched closer to the two hour duration I’m accustomed to. Defensive […]
full_text: FLOWERY BRANCH, GEORGIA - MAY 27: Tua Tagovailoa #1 of the Atlanta Falcons runs through drills during OTA's at IBM Performance Field on May 27, 2026 in Flowery Branch, Georgia. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Falcons returned to the practice field on Monday after a day off on Sunday, and delivered arguably the best practice of training camp so far. With the pads on for the first time, energy was high and we got the longest practice session—which inched closer to the two hour duration I’m accustomed to. Defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich returned to the sideline, and Tua Tagovailoa returned to full team work. Here are my notes from Day 5 of Falcons training camp. Offense QB Tua Tagovailoa returned to 11-on-11 and had arguably the best pass of the day, a well-layered throw to Drake London over the leaping Christian Harris. He only had a handful of reps, but it was good to see him back out there. QB Michael Penix Jr. had his best practice of camp thus far, looking much sharper on his short throws and connecting on a few lovely deep passes. The final play of the day was a deep bomb to WR Antwane Wells Jr. that was placed perfectly. QB Jack Strand continues to take chances and looks a lot more aggressive than the veteran QB Cooper Rush. Strand has looked a little frazzled under pressure compared to Rush, but did show off his escapability with a nice run after getting out of the pocket. I do think Strand was more impressive overall today than Rush. WR Zachariah Branch wasn’t slowed down one bit by the addition of pads, looking just as dominant in 1-on-1s and finding ways to get open in the team drills. He continues to have a great camp. Zachariah Branch vs AJ Woods #Falcons pic.twitter.com/hkBdyYZkGI — Kevin Knight (@FalcoholicKevin) August 3, 2026 WR Jahan Dotson is clearly the WR2 and has looked the part, coming on strong over the past two practices. He’s versatile and showed off some great hands working entirely with the starters. Among the other wide receivers, Chris Blair continues to look the most impressive. His size stands out in a room full of smaller, speedier guys. WR Chris Blair with the catch against CB CJ Henderson #Falcons pic.twitter.com/GYARggybEO — Kevin Knight (@FalcoholicKevin) August 3, 2026 TE Kyle Pitts had a down day, with a couple of drops that could’ve been really nice plays. He did put on some nice moves on a screen pass that actually picked up a nice chunk of yardage. RB Cash Jones continues to show up, with a nice run and an impressive wheel route catch for about 20 yards against LB JD Bertrand. Defense The defense didn’t dominate quite as much as on Saturday, but they still looked like the better unit overall. The pass rush, in particular, was making things very difficult for Strand and Rush. I tracked Samson Ebukam, Cameron Thomas, and Keshawn Banks with sacks, along with Jessie Bates who got one on a blitz. With Bijan not out there, the defense has also been pretty smothering against the run. Christian Harris , Maason Smith , Chris Williams all had TFLs. Avieon Terrell also showed off his physicality, notching a couple of nice stuffs. Speaking of CB Avieon Terrell , this was his best day in coverage. His tight coverage on one play led to a coverage sack for Cameron Thomas. He’s been better in team sessions than 1-on-1s and is seemingly making his way up the depth chart. CB Clark Phillips III had a strong day in coverage and seems to have found his home back outside. CB Clark Phillips III with the PBU against WR Dylan Drummond #Falcons pic.twitter.com/Kj9alzVUI1 — Kevin Knight (@FalcoholicKevin) August 3, 2026 The Falcons were trying out a lot of different blitz packages, which meant a lot of rotation with the LBs. We saw Harold Perkins and Kendal Daniels continue to mix in to various looks throughout the day. There’s a lot of rotation up front on the defensive line. Throughout practice I saw Jalon Walker, Samson Ebukam, Cameron Thomas, and Bralen Trice all getting reps with the “starters” on the edge. Inside, Brandon Dorlus, LaCale London, Maason Smith, Da’Shawn Hand, and Chris Williams were all a part of the rotation. James Pearce Jr. continues to work primarily with the depth groups. The slot cornerback battle appears wide open. A.J. Woods got the first snaps once again today, but Darnay Holmes continues to factor in. Avieon Terrell got more snaps inside today than outside, but is still splitting his reps. Notably, it looked like Natrone Brooks was back working with the safeties today. Updates This was the longest practice so far, inching closer to the 2 hours we’re used to. The intensity was noticeably higher with the pads on. OT Wanya Morris showed up late in practice with a knee brace and looked a little hobbled. Not sure if the knee brace is new, but he didn’t look healthy. I’ll try to get more information on what is going on with him tomorrow. We got the first session from veteran kicker Nick Folk , and he looked sharp, connecting on kicks from 48 and 52. CB Billy Bowman Jr. was out working and running on the rehab field with his helmet on for the first time since I’ve been here. It was good to see him out there and he looks to be getting closer. Tuesday’s practice is without pads and actually in the afternoon for the first time, but we’ll be back to pads on Wednesday. Stay tuned for our live show this afternoon, as Adnan Ikic will be joining me to bring you our report from Day 5. Otherwise, we’ll see you all for Day 6!
