title: Cincinnati Bengals roster 2026: Dax Hill, Jonathan Allen, Connor Lew are Hidden Gems
summary: It was not too long ago that the Cincinnati Bengals were right up top in the AFC pecking order. In 2021 and 2022, they got as close as you can get to winning a Super Bowl without actually winning it. There was the 23-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams in Super Bowl LVI at […]
full_text: Cincinnati Bengals cornerback Dax Hill (23) catches a pass during the Cincinnati Bengals Training Camp 2026 at Kettering Practice Field in Cincinnati on Thursday, July 30, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co It was not too long ago that the Cincinnati Bengals were right up top in the AFC pecking order. In 2021 and 2022, they got as close as you can get to winning a Super Bowl without actually winning it. There was the 23-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams in Super Bowl LVI at the end of the 2021 season and the 23-20 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs in the 2022 AFC Championship game. Of course, after those two 23-20 games in a span of less than a year, things started to come apart. Joe Burrow’s health became more of a concern in 2023 and 2025, and when Burrow played at a thermonuclear level in 2024, he did so with a Lou Anarumo defense that ranked 25th in points allowed and 27th in DVOA . Last season, Burrow played in just eight games, and in the first half of the season, Al Golden’s defense was one of the worst… like, ever. According to FTN’s data, Cincinnati’s defensive DVOA of 30.1% in Weeks 1-9 was the worst in the history of the metric, which currently goes back to 1977. Running back Chase Brown and receiver Ja’Marr Chase were yowling about said defense in October , and for good reason. Then, it all turned around. From Week 10 through the end of the season, the Bengals improved their Defensive DVOA to -2.2% (Defensive DVOA is better when it’s negative), up from 32nd to 13th. And though the sins of the season’s first half would not be erased by that improvement — the 2025 Bengals finished 30th in Defensive DVOA behind only the Dallas Cowboys and the New York Jets — there was enough on the bone for management to spend in both draft capital and actual dollars to improve things on that side of the ball. Hence, the trade for ex-New York Giants game-wrecker Dexter Lawrence, as well as the signings of former Seattle Seahawks edge-rusher Boye Mafe, veteran defensive lineman Jonathan Allen, former Kansas City Chiefs safety Bryan Cook, and veteran defensive back Kyle Dugger. Adding Texas A&M edge-rusher Cashius Howell and Washington cornerback Tacario Davis in the second and third rounds of the 2026 draft should provide even more enforcement potential. So, here’s what the plan for the Bengals this season seems to be: Bank on a healthy Joe Burrow and all of his weapons, and give the defense enough juice to be league average or better after that historical awfulness. It worked not too long ago, and it could work again. For that to happen, of course, the Bengals will need the best possible performance from everybody on the roster. To that end, I’ve identified three Hidden Gems for the 2026 team — one underrated veteran, one underrated free agent, and one underrated draft pick. Here are the Hidden Gems for your 2026 Cincinnati Bengals. Underrated veteran: DB Dax Hill A primary reason for the aforementioned defensive improvement in the second half of the 2025 season was the decision to move Dax Hill outside from the slot more often. Since the Bengals took the Michigan alum with the 31st overall pick in the 2022 draft, Hill has alternated between the two spots, with varying degrees of distinction. 2024 was a complicated season for Hill: he missed all but the first five games with a knee injury, but he came back strong, especially when the team needed someone to bookend the estimable DJ Turner II. From Weeks 1-11 last season, Hill took just 20% of his 666 ( Iron Maiden riff here ) snaps outside; the rest of the time, he was either a slot defender or a box guy. But starting in Week 12 against the New England Patriots, Hill’s outside reps increased exponentially. 76% of his 366 reps in that time period came on the outside, and when targeted there, Hill allowed 12 catches on 19 targets for 6.7 yards per catch, no touchdowns, no interceptions, four pass breakups, and an opponent passer rating of 76.2. Most importantly. Hill’s outside deployment told opponents that they couldn’t just avoid Turner and get away with THAT all day long. If you blinked or looked away for a second, you probably missed the @Bengals ' massive uptick in defensive efficiency in the second half of the 2025 season. Moving Dax Hill from slot to outside had a lot to do with it. pic.twitter.com/kMtGnSQuiV — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) July 30, 2026 After the season, the Bengals named Hill their winner of the NFL’s Ed Block Courage Award , which credits players who show “professionalism, great strength and dedication” in the face of adversity. “I want to thank the entire organization and my teammates for thinking highly of me in coming back from my injury,” Hill said. “Representing the team well, coming back, and making an impact was my big focus. I thank everybody for being in my corner, and I’m happy being back with the guys.” “There is not a more deserving player than Dax Hill for the Ed Block Courage Award,” said Bengals Director of Sports Medicine/Head Athletic Trainer Matt Summers. “Dax is a very consistent ‘everyday’ guy. His unwavering work ethic and trust in the rehab plan allowed him to return to the field in 2025 without hesitation. Dax is also very gracious with the time he commits to community service, and his humility further reflects the values he poses for his teammates to vote him as this year’s recipient.” If Hill’s on-field community service continues to be the ability to shut receivers down as that outside guy, that’s one more box for the team to check off as they fight for relevance again. Underrated free agent: IDL Jonathan Allen Dexter Lawrence was obviously the big move the Bengals made this offseason, but it wasn’t the only contract signed to bolster the defensive line. Getting nine-year veteran Jonathan Allen on a two-year, $25 million contract with $7.5 million guaranteed should provide some sneaky dividends. Last season in Brian Flores’ crazy-quilt defense for the Minnesota Vikings, Allen had four sacks, 34 pressures, 44 solo tackles, 34 stops, and seven tackles for loss. That was Allen’s first season in Minnesota after eight with the Washington (YOUR NAME HERE) franchise, which selected him with the 17th overall pick in the 2017 draft out of Alabama. At his peak, Allen lived up to all that draft capital spent, and while he may not be the pressure machine he was in 2021 and 2022, he’s not that far off. At 6’3” and 300 pounds, he brings all the movement skills and a surprising amount of power to displace double teams for his size. As long as Sexy Dexy is on the field, Allen won’t see as many doubles as he did in 2025 — 190— and 17 of his 34 pressures came when he had more than one guy on him. So, there could be a bump in the numbers for the veteran. And the run defense is already *chef’s kiss.* Jonathan Allen spending time in yo' backfield. Moving Allen around with Sexy Dexy as the epicenter should be fun. @Bengals pic.twitter.com/7rh2meKKGk — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) July 30, 2026 Allen is certainly happy about the prospects for that interior line. “I don’t think there’s ever been a guy to play like Dexter,” Allen said in June. “Dexter is a unique guy, and I’m just excited for the opportunity. “It’s funny. After I left Minnesota (last season), I just sat down and had to really think what I wanted. I’d be lying if I said I didn’t want to come up here and put up great numbers. That proves your worth and why they brought you in. But, honestly, I just want to play meaningful football in December, and I want to help the team any way I can. I believe if I do that, the numbers will come. “At this point in my career, it’s all about winning, man.” It’s been a while since anybody voiced that reason for signing with the Bengals, but here we are, and it could happen more quickly with Allen’s contributions. Underrated draft pick: Center Connor Lew You obviously don’t know how NFL teams feel about your draft binkies until one actually selects one of them. In the case of…

title: Tee Higgins and Dexter Lawrence snubbed from NFL Top 100 Players ranking
summary: When I was in middle school and high school, my springs and summers were spent anticipating the weekly episodes of the NFL Top 100 Players going into the upcoming season. Ten players per week were revealed on NFL Network, and there were reaction shows right after each episode. The list was voted exclusively by the […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - JULY 29: Tee Higgins #5 of the Cincinnati Bengals performs during the Cincinnati Bengals Training Camp at Kettering Health Practice Fields on July 29, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images When I was in middle school and high school, my springs and summers were spent anticipating the weekly episodes of the NFL Top 100 Players going into the upcoming season. Ten players per week were revealed on NFL Network, and there were reaction shows right after each episode. The list was voted exclusively by the players, and they were usually spot on with the rankings every year. But this year, the list is drawing major criticism on Twitter. Lamar Jackson is ranked No. 69. Okay, yes, Jackson missed four games last year and wasn’t as dynamic as he was in 2023 or 2024, but the players are saying there are 68 players better than Jackson? Going into this season, they think there are nearly 70 players better than two-time NFL MVP Lamar Jackson? Look, availability is the best ability, and players do pay attention to production. A player’s whole career, though, should be taken into account when compiling this annual list. From a Bengals’ perspective, Joe Burrow checked in at No. 44 last week. So, there are 43 players better than Joe Burrow? Yeah, sure. But the ridiculousness doesn’t stop there. Tee Higgins and Dexter Lawrence didn’t even make the list. They were ranked just outside the top 100, as revealed early this week. Players who just missed the NFL Top 100… 110: Tyler Warren 109: Tee Higgins 108: Brian Branch 107: Devon Witherspoon 106: Jameson Williams 105: Dexter Lawrence 104: Chris Lindstrom 103: CJ Stroud 102: Lane Johnson 101: Mike Evans pic.twitter.com/bjfSYLDg0V — NFL (@NFL) August 3, 2026 Hold on… so the players who voted think there are 100 players better than BOTH Higgins and Lawrence? Humor me, a little bit. Tee Higgins absolutely justified the Bengals paying him with a terrific 2025 season. All he did, playing with three different starting quarterbacks, was score 11 receiving touchdowns on 59 receptions for 846 yards. Lawrence may have only had a half-sack last season. But as we have talked about at length this offseason, a change of scenery could be exactly what he needs to get back to his beast-like production from the middle of the defensive line. Let’s not forget he had nine sacks in 2024, and that was only in 12 games. Look, players and coaches know the NFL game better than anybody. That’s why the NFL Top 100 Players list used to matter significantly. It was a refreshing concept to have the players be the only ones voting. But this year, the list is coming into serious question and is being heavily criticized. For the players who voted, thinking there are 100 better players than Tee Higgins and Dexter Lawrence is lunacy. And 43 better players than Joe Burrow? Come on.

title: Bengals training camp Day 6 News and discussion
summary: The news from Monday’s training camp session was once again about the Cincinnati Bengals’ defense making plays. After an offseason of additions, this is music to fan’s ears. As the pads came on, the impact of free agent signing Jonathan Allen and the blockbuster trade for Dexter Lawrence II was felt all over the practice […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - JULY 29: Joe Burrow #9 of the Cincinnati Bengals performs during the Cincinnati Bengals Training Camp at Kettering Health Practice Fields on July 29, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images The news from Monday’s training camp session was once again about the Cincinnati Bengals’ defense making plays. After an offseason of additions, this is music to fan’s ears. As the pads came on, the impact of free agent signing Jonathan Allen and the blockbuster trade for Dexter Lawrence II was felt all over the practice fields outside of Paycor Stadium. While the performance of the defense has been applauded, some are wondering if concern for the offense is warranted. Reports state that Zac Taylor’s offense has been operating from under center more than we’ve seen in any training camp, but the results seem mixed. While the run game had success Monday, the defense appeared to win more of the passing situations. We’re in early August, so it isn’t time to panic about the offense, but coming out of training camp with confidence and momentum could do wonders for a defense that ranked at or near the bottom of the NFL in 2025. Bengals News Dexter Lawrence making instant impact at Bengals camp: ‘Honestly, he’s been terrorizing practice’ “A maligned Bengals defense loaded up on offseason upgrades to the tune of a practice group that offensive players say is more intense and competitive than Cincinnati’s defense flashed last training camp.“ Could one player make that big of a difference on a defense? It appears that it could. Add that to the other offseason additions and it is easy to see why the offense can see a difference in the 2026 defense as training camp ramps up. Joe Burrow, Bengals find camaraderie on unusual battlefield “Cincinnati’s first week of training camp has featured a few spirited practices, a noted practice scuffle and an intense edge from a team sick of missing the playoffs. But as it has looked to put the rest of the AFC North in check in 2026, the first days of the season have also featured a chessboard.“ Plenty of work takes place on the field during training camp, but connections are made in the locker room just as much, if not more. Players are spending tons of time with one another and finding ways to connect beyond the game are crucial. This year, the thing that is bringing them together appears to be a chessboard. Training Camp Report | A Dax Hill Vignette As Bengals Put On The Pads “I feel like we can play a lot faster, be more confident and play faster knowing the ball has to come out. Simple as that,” Monday was reportedly a great day for Dax Hill. With all the talk about DJ Turner II’s contract, Hill is entering a contract year as well. Hill has battled injuries and played several different positions in his time in Cincinnati, but that experience and versatility were on full display for the first day in pads. Bengals experience false alarm in first padded practice of training camp, Joe Burrow and the offense struggle in specific area “The 25 year-old is eligible for a big-time payday before the regular season begins, which is when Cincinnati traditionally finalize its biggest internal contracts. He’s been completely locked in despite the potential distraction and it’s great to see him push through what appeared to be a cramp.” A scare at training camp to say the least. For DJ Turner II, it comes while contract negotiations are presumably going on behind the scenes. Thankfully, Hill was able to get back on the field quickly. Meanwhile, the Bengals’ offense struggled in an area it would really benefit them to succeed at.

title: Colbie Young has big day at training camp; says he’s learning from 2 Hall of Fame receivers
summary: What can we expect to see from Colbie Young in his rookie campaign? The Cincinnati Bengals’ fourth-round draft pick out of Georgia was relatively quiet during the opening week of training camp. However, Young had his best day of camp on Monday afternoon. That included a spectacular sideline catch from Joe Flacco, going up and […]
full_text: Jul 29, 2026; Cincinnati, OH, USA; Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Colbie Young (86) catches a pass during training camp at Kettering Health Practice Fields. Mandatory Credit: Katie Stratman-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect What can we expect to see from Colbie Young in his rookie campaign? The Cincinnati Bengals’ fourth-round draft pick out of Georgia was relatively quiet during the opening week of training camp. However, Young had his best day of camp on Monday afternoon. That included a spectacular sideline catch from Joe Flacco, going up and high-pointing the football over the defender. Bengals rookie wide receiver Colbie Young makes his first splash play of camp. A high point reception from Joe Flacco on the sideline. pic.twitter.com/wxasvnZONB — Joe Danneman (@FOX19Joe) August 3, 2026 At 6-foot-4 and around 220 pounds, Young has excellent size for the receiver position. This allows him to make contested catches consistently over cornerbacks. He is more of a big-play weapon than incumbent wide receiver No. 3 Andrei Iosivas. At Georgia, over 75% of Young’s receptions resulted in either a first down or a touchdown. He was known for running a lot of posts and 9-routes for the Bulldogs. Young added a touchdown reception during Monday’s practice. Both plays, including the aforementioned sideline catch, came from passes from Joe Flacco. Joe Flacco connects with rookie WR Colbie Young who finds the end zone pic.twitter.com/RZOgty6Psj — Andrew Fo 𝕏 Miller (@AndrewFoxMiller) August 3, 2026 Iosivas continues working with Joe Burrow and the first-team offense. That likely means he begins the season as one of the starting receivers. However, I think Colbie Young could ultimately start cutting into his snaps throughout the season. With Iosivas having a 13% drop rate in 2025, combined with entering the final year of his contract, the Bengals would be wise to work in Young more and more as the season gets underway. Young spoke with the media after practice. He discussed how he can sit back and learn from what he believes are two future Hall of Famers at the receiver position. “I think I am one of the luckiest receivers to get drafted,” Young said. “I got two Hall of Fame receivers in front of me that I get to learn from. I don’t have to be rushed in, but when my number is called, I have to go out and perform.” Colbie Young high pointed a ball from Joe Flacco and made a terrific catch on the sideline in 11s. Also caught a slant in end zone from Joe Burrow in front of Dax Hill. Good day for the rookie. pic.twitter.com/30O0qIPA73 — Mike Petraglia (@Trags) August 3, 2026 It will be important for Young to impress during preseason action. He will get his first opportunity next Thursday when the Bengals face the Lions in their first preseason game of the year.

title: Andrei Iosivas is showing improved speed and separation in training camp
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals get plenty of press surrounding their wide receiver room. With a bona fide superstar in Ja’Marr Chase and a WR1-talent like Tee Higgins playing opposite Chase, the Bengals boast a duo most teams in the league almost certainly envy. For years, Tyler Boyd was the third receiver in the rotation during the beginning of […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 27: Andrei Iosivas #80 of the Cincinnati Bengals scores a touchdown during an NFL football game against the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium on November 27, 2025 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cincinnati Bengals get plenty of press surrounding their wide receiver room. With a bona fide superstar in Ja’Marr Chase and a WR1-talent like Tee Higgins playing opposite Chase, the Bengals boast a duo most teams in the league almost certainly envy. For years, Tyler Boyd was the third receiver in the rotation during the beginning of the Joe Burrow era. Since he’s moved on, Andrei Iosivas has been given the bulk of the opportunity to hold down the role of third wide receiver. After being a track star at Princeton, he has seen his fair share of snaps in the Bengals’ offense. While he hasn’t reached the level Boyd was at, reports from early in training camp say that Iosivas looks even faster as he heads into a contract year. “He’s playing with confidence, and he’s playing fast. He looks really fast,” offensive coordinator Dan Pitcher told Bengals.com’s Geoff Hobson . “He’s been fast, but he’s playing really fast. Taking advantage of the opportunities that come his way. Even on plays he hasn’t been targeted, he’s had some really good releases where he separated from bump man.” For all the attention Higgins and Chase command, a breakout season from Iosivas, paired with a healthy Mike Gesicki, could make this potent offense even more dangerous. Iosivas did have five drops last season, with some of them coming in crucial moments, so he will need to clean that up. Rookie wide receiver Colbie Young has impressed as well, and if drops are an issue for Iosivas again, Young could challenge him for snaps. Iosivas seems to have a good mindset going into what could be his last year in Cincinnati. “I just want to play and have fun. That’s my biggest thing,” Iosivas said. “Just out there having fun, not caring about anything. Just going.” It is too early to predict what the future holds for him in Cincinnati, but Iosivas will be eager to have a strong season so he can cash in during free agency in 2027.
author: Drew Garrison

title: Ja’Marr Chase knows what he and the Bengals need to do to recapture 2021 magic
summary: Every Cincinnati Bengals fan has heard or thought about how this offseason feels very similar to 2021. This offseason, the Bengals were heavily active in free agency after a disastrous season the year before, much like how active they were in free agency in 2021 after Joe Burrow got his knee shredded 10 games into […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OH - DECEMBER 26: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase (1) runs with the football during a game between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Baltimore Ravens on December 26, 2021, at Paul Brown Stadium in Cincinnati, OH. (Photo by Robin Alam/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Every Cincinnati Bengals fan has heard or thought about how this offseason feels very similar to 2021. This offseason, the Bengals were heavily active in free agency after a disastrous season the year before, much like how active they were in free agency in 2021 after Joe Burrow got his knee shredded 10 games into his rookie season in 2020. In addition, the schedule this season has many parallels to the 2021 schedule: Week 1 at home against an NFC opponent, Week 3 at Pittsburgh at 1:00, Week 4 at home against Jacksonville. Sound familiar? It should. But the biggest thing about the 2021 Bengals was how explosive they were offensively, how easy they made it look to air the ball out and take the top off the defense. Even with the success of the last four seasons on offense, they haven’t been as explosive on that side of the ball. Ja’Marr Chase knows this, and he made it clear to start training camp that the Bengals need to recapture their explosive nature offensively, the same explosive offense that got former Baltimore Ravens defensive coordinator Don Martindale fired after the 2021 season. “Defenses are adjusting to us,” Chase stated. “That’s what they’re supposed to do. It’s our job for us to get better, be better than last year, and make those adjustments to be more explosive. “We’ve just got to see it, recognize it and be able to adjust for the next play.” In that 2021 season, the Bengals put up 41 points on the Ravens in both games. Joe Burrow threw for 941 combined yards and seven touchdowns. Ja’Marr Chase had 15 receptions for 326 yards and a touchdown. “Me and Joe are already talking about how we can make explosives,” Chase said. “And when I finally get it in camp, it’s just, how can I react to it when I see it in the game? So, we’re practicing now, and when the game comes, we see it and attack it. And it’s explosive.” If the Bengals can take the top off defenses this season, good luck trying to stop them on offense. With all five starters returning on the offensive line, that could lead to more plays that take time to unfold down the field. If Burrow can sit in the pocket and let Chase fly down the field, good luck trying to keep the top on your defense.
author: Alex Frank

title: Bengals training camp Day 5 News and discussion
summary: We have seen a bit of fight from the Cincinnati Bengals defense early in training camp. The team certainly did quite a bit to improve that side of the ball in the offseason, and we have seen that show up in Boye Mafe making some early pressures. However, we have also seen players like Demetrius […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 12: Defensive coordinator Al Golden of the Cincinnati Bengals looks on during the first quarter in the game against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field on October 12, 2025 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images We have seen a bit of fight from the Cincinnati Bengals defense early in training camp. The team certainly did quite a bit to improve that side of the ball in the offseason, and we have seen that show up in Boye Mafe making some early pressures. However, we have also seen players like Demetrius Knight Jr. and Barrett Carter make plays at linebacker. Is it time to panic about the offense? Definitely not. Quarterback Joe Burrow has still had moments of absolute brilliant ball placement, and there were days like this even last offseason when the defense got the better of them. This is the time to experiment with some things, and Burrow and company are doing plenty of that. Let us know in the comments your feelings on this year’s squad after a few days of training camp to digest. Bengals News Training Camp Report | Boye Mafe Finds A Home; Erick All Jr.’s Wait Ends Monday “One thing about me, I’m out there working trying to crack my craft,” Mafe said. “Camp is where you fine-tune your craft. You work all summer on different moves, different ways to elevate your game. See what works, see what doesn’t work, see what you can take into the season.” Mafe is carrying plenty of expectations to see his production expand with a bigger role. His current approach suggests it is a good bet for the team to make. The entire defense improving obviously involves more than him stepping up, but him becoming an EDGE who can consistently pressure the quarterback is a fairly large piece of that. Quick Hits | Jalen Davis Strikes Again; Connor Lew Debut; 2 Cincy Kids At Camp “You get the happy nerves. I haven’t had contact since the end of October,” said Lew, alluding to the torn ACL he suffered against Missouri. “We’re at the stage where we’re not ahead of schedule or behind schedule. It’s just day-to-day, and they told me I could go out there and get full-speed contact. It felt really good.” Davis certainly keeps having his name pop up. The first was the scuffle he and wide receiver Ja’Marr Chase had on Day 1 of training camp. This time he made an opportune turnover. He has never made it easy on this coaching staff to cut him, but now he is making it hard for them to keep him off the field. Why Bengals keep dropping Boye Mafe, Cashius Howell in pass coverage “That’s something I am trying to work on to get more comfortable with,” Howell told Geoff Hobson of Bengals.com. “My primary thing is rushing the passer and playing on the line of scrimmage, but that is something I am trying to actively work on and actively make sure I’m getting better at day by day.” It does make sense that Mafe and Howell are not as prolific in coverage as they are rushing the passer. It also feels like offenses have caught up to this tactic. Namely, players like Burrow, Patrick Mahomes, Josh Allen… etc., all have seen this for years now. It is nice to sprinkle in, but the key is you need to be able to rush the passer into making a mistake when you drop a defensive lineman into coverage. If you can’t, then the quarterback can wait for a receiver to find the hole in whatever zone that lineman is covering. Mafe and Howell are never going to be good enough in coverage to make a play defensively if the quarterback has all day to throw. To try and make the point a bit clearer. If Mafe and Howell are considered to have a D in coverage, they are good enough as a surprise defensive lineman if the quarterback has to act quickly because of the pass rush. Becoming a D+ or even a C-graded coverage player isn’t enough of an improvement for them to be good enough if the quarterback has even a decent amount of time in the pocket. Bengals’ Early-Season Test Just Got Tougher After Texans’ Latest Move Clowney gives Houston another proven weapon to unleash against Joe Burrow and Cincinnati’s offensive line. Danielle Hunter and Will Anderson Jr. combined for 27 sacks last season, leaving Houston with two defenders capable of taking over a game from opposite sides of the defensive front. Unfortunately, an already good defense gets better in the AFC. There were reports that Clowney was also talking with the Cleveland Browns about a return. Even without Myles Garrett, that defensive line is still fairly scary with Jared Verse taking his spot. So they will only have to see him once on a loaded defensive line instead of twice.

title: Browns roster 2026: Dillon Gabriel, Quincy Williams, Emmanuel McNeil-Warren are underrated
summary: Okay, so. We don’t need to torture avid Cleveland Browns fans with the quarterback jokes, because they’ve all been told. We don’t need to bag on Deshaun Watson or Jimmy Haslam, as much as those two individuals have presented legit reasons for mockery and scorn. And we don’t really need to go over all the […]
full_text: Okay, so. We don’t need to torture avid Cleveland Browns fans with the quarterback jokes , because they’ve all been told. We don’t need to bag on Deshaun Watson or Jimmy Haslam, as much as those two individuals have presented legit reasons for mockery and scorn. And we don’t really need to go over all the changes that happened with the coaching staff per se — everyone visiting this fine site likely already knows that Kevin Stefanski was replaced by Todd Monken as head coach and offensive shot-caller, while Jim Schwartz was replaced by Mike Rutenberg as the man in charge of the defense. Instead, let’s dive into reasons for optimism that have very little to do with the quarterback thing because we’ll go there in a minute. The 2026 Browns can benefit from EVP/general manager Andrew Berry’s recent personnel moves, including a 2025 draft that appears to be long-term great. The defense under Schwartz was generally anywhere from pretty good to really good, and outside of Myles Garrett, most of the key pieces are returning. It’s not as if Jared Verse, who came to Cleveland in the Garrett trade, is chopped liver, either — he’s just not a lead-pipe first-ballot Hall of Famer lock like No. 95. At least not yet. The 2026 draft brought two estimable weapons in receivers KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston, and the offensive line underwent a neat transformation this offseason with first-round tackle Spencer Fano and free agents Zion Johnson, Elgton Jenkins, and Tytus Howard. 2025 Hidden Gem Teven Jenkins announced his presence with authority last season, so the front five should be very solid over time. Rookie running back Quinshon Judkins was an absolute boss when healthy. Basically, the 2026 Browns appear to be one of those teams that are just a quarterback away from contention. Which is a bit like saying that you’re one Eddie Van Halen away from being Van Halen, but one does the best one can with what one has. Wherever the Browns are headed this season, they’ll need the best possible from everyone on the roster — not just the big names. To that end, I’ve identified three Hidden Gems — one underrated veteran, one underrated free agent, and one underrated draft pick. And I’m sure the underrated veteran won’t inspire some agita in the comments. All I ask is that you hear me out on this one. Underrated veteran: QB Dillon Gabriel The Browns should not expect top-tier quarterback play in the 2026 season. We’re pretty sure about that. Once you’ve lowered the bar accordingly in that regard, what’s the next most crucial thing for the game’s most important position? For the Browns, situational consistency could be it. And that’s why Dillon Gabriel could be the team’s best option this season . It started in 2024, when Gabriel was Bo Nix’s replacement at Oregon. Overall in that season, Gabriel completed 326 of 451 passes for 3,854 yards, 30 touchdowns, six interceptions, and a passer rating of 114.6. Good numbers, but it’s how Gabriel got to those numbers that impressed me. When under pressure: 56 of 104 for 892 yards, eight touchdowns, one interception, and a passer rating of 104.3. When blitzed: 103 of 142 for 1,286 yards, 15 touchdowns, one interception, and a passer rating of 132.5. On passes of 20+ air yards: 27 of 49 for 960 yards, eight touchdowns, one interception, and a passer rating of 131.9. Throwing from the pocket: 275 of 361 for 3,137 yards, 22 touchdowns, three interceptions, and a passer rating of 118.6. Throwing outside the pocket: 51 of 86 for 720 yards, eight touchdowns, three interceptions, and a passer rating of 102.9. Gabriel had to wait for his shots with the Browns in 2025, but when he got them, he did deliver. Overall, he completed 110 of 185 passes for 937 yards, seven touchdowns, two interceptions, and a passer rating of 80.8. Again, it was how Gabriel got to those numbers that stood out in a quarterback room that couldn’t get out of its own way most of the time. When under pressure: 32 of 63 for 320 yards, four touchdowns, one interception, and a passer rating of 80.1. When blitzed: 37 of 63 for 313 yards, two touchdowns, one interception, and a passer rating of 75.7. On passes of 20+ air yards: 2 of 8 for 44 yards, one touchdown, one interception, and a passer rating of 50.0 (okay, this needs some improvement). Throwing from the pocket: 97 of 157 for 767 yards, six touchdowns, one interception, and a passer rating of 84.0. Throwing outside the pocket: 13 of 28 for 170 yards, one touchdown, one interception, and a passer rating of 63.1. Does this bring to mind Tua Tagovailoa as a point guard-style quarterback who’s pretty good at distributing the ball all over the place, as long as you don’t ask him to scald defenses with deep balls, and rely too much on functional mobility? Before you laugh at any Tua comps, think about how much Tagovailoa at his best would have presented a marked improvement over what Shedeur Sanders or Joe Flacco did with the Browns last season, and certainly what Deshaun Watson would have forced us to watch had he been healthy. It’s not that Dillon Gabriel is the guy to break the Browns’ ridiculous quarterback curse. For the 2026 season, that’s not the point. The point is that if you ask Gabriel to limit his deeper shots to the intermediate level (on throws of 10-19 yards last season, he completed 19 of 44 for 305 yards, four touchdowns, no interceptions, and a passer rating of 97.3), and let him cook under center ( where he did see a relatively nice uptick in EPA/Play )… well, maybe the Browns could make enough of that to avoid stranding their defense again, and actually win some ballgames in successive order. explain to my why and how dillon gabriel isn't the browns' best quarterback yes, i know the bar is buried underground pic.twitter.com/1iu6Rvn41g — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) August 1, 2026 Underrated free agent: LB Quincy Williams New coaches love to bring players with whom they’re familiar to their new stops, and new Browns defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg happily brought linebacker Quincy Williams to Cleveland once he had signed on as Jim Schwartz’s replacement. Williams, the brother of former New York Jets and current Dallas Cowboys interior defensive lineman Quinnen Williams, was selected in the third round of the 2019 draft by the Jacksonville Jaguars out of Murray State, and Rutenberg was the Jags’ assistant linebackers coach at the time. When Rutenberg became the Jets’ linebackers coach in 2021, he brought Williams onto the roster after Williams failed to make final cuts with Jacksonville in August of that year. This reunion should not come as a surprise. “That’s my dog. He’s like my brother,” Williams said of Rutenberg once Williams had signed his two-year, $13 million contract with $9.5 million guaranteed. “First thing before we talk about football, the biggest thing is Rudy cares about the heart. What I do off the field affects what I do on the field. So, he wanted to tackle both things as far as what I do on the field, so I can show up as myself — show up as this personality always smiling as me, show up every single day at work like that. So, he cares about that a lot. And then on the field, as long as we take care off the field, on the field should be easy. He taught me every single thing I know as far as the linebacker positions in the league. He was with me the two teams I’ve been on, so we have a good relationship.” Williams has never been what you would call a star in coverage, but when it comes to facing forward, blowing up run fits, and going after the quarterback, he’s got it all on point. Last season for a Jets defense that was generally quite abysmal, Williams racked up four sacks, 12 pressures, eight tackles for loss, 61 solo tackles, and 42 stops. For a Browns defense that will be looking to place pressure players around Jared Verse as it once tried to do for Myles Garrett, Williams’ blitz efficiency from all over the front seven should be a major addition. title: NFL QB tiers: Where former Browns QBs rank versus current Cleveland QBs
summary: Normally, when training camp starts in the NFL, we see the end of ranking season. Throughout the offseason, we covered all sorts of Cleveland Browns-related rankings. Whether it was multiple power rankings, 2026 NFL draft grades/rankings, where stars like Carson Schwesinger, Denzel Ward, Harold Fannin Jr., and Quinshon Judkins were ranked among their positions, or […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 30: Baker Mayfield #6 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Jacoby Brissett #7 of the Arizona Cardinals hug after the game at Raymond James Stadium on November 30, 2025 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Julio Aguilar/Getty Images) | Getty Images Normally, when training camp starts in the NFL, we see the end of ranking season. Throughout the offseason, we covered all sorts of Cleveland Browns-related rankings. Whether it was multiple power rankings , 2026 NFL draft grades/rankings , where stars like Carson Schwesinger , Denzel Ward , Harold Fannin Jr. , and Quinshon Judkins were ranked among their positions, or where the Browns young core was placed among the rest of the league , ranking season was vast but seemed mostly over. With training camp in full swing, one more set of rankings, tiers really, is now available. As we covered, Mike Sando’s QB tiers do not speak highly of QBs Shedeur Sanders and Deshaun Watson . There is more hope connected to Sanders from the 50 coaches and executives, but he is also ranked at the bottom of the list of 35 quarterbacks. Given Cleveland’s history, it is interesting to note that two former Browns quarterbacks also made the list , but not former playoff QB Joe Flacco . Sando’s tiers have Baker Mayfield tied with Sam Darnold for 14th overall in the second tier. As Mayfield looks to enter free agency , his career has been an interesting up-and-down roller coaster with another season to prove he is worthy of a top-tier contract. Fitting squarely between Watson and Sanders in the rankings is former Cleveland QB Jacoby Brissett . The Arizona Cardinals starter heading into the 2026 season, Brissett negotiated a raise on his contract this offseason but is still ranked near the bottom of the veteran starters in the NFL. Joining Watson, Sanders, and Brissett in the bottom five are two recent early first-round picks: Michael Penix Jr. (32) and JJ McCarthy (34). Are you surprised at any of the rankings listed above? Did you expect Mayfield and/or Brissett to be higher on the list? Does Penix and McCarthy being ranked so low give you even more concern about drafting a quarterback high in the future? title: About Browns QB Shedeur Sanders: ‘I’d sleep like a baby if I got to play him every week’
summary: Is the above comment about Cleveland Browns QB Shedeur Sanders a strong one to title this piece? Of course it is. Is it accurate? At least it is what one defensive coordinator believes. The Browns QB competition is off and running. All we know, according to HC Todd Monken, is that a lot of things […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - APRIL 21: Deshaun Watson #4, Shedeur Sanders #2 and Dillon Gabriel #8 of the Cleveland Browns run a drill during a voluntary veteran minicamp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on April 21, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images Is the above comment about Cleveland Browns QB Shedeur Sanders a strong one to title this piece? Of course it is. Is it accurate? At least it is what one defensive coordinator believes. The Browns QB competition is off and running. All we know, according to HC Todd Monken, is that a lot of things still have to be installed in Week 2’s schedule and QB Dillon Gabriel has earned more reps . Day 5 was a lot like the previous days at Cleveland’s training camp , with a few exciting plays and a lot of concern about the quarterback play . From the outside looking in, the Browns quarterback room does not have a lot of believers. In Mike Sando’s annual QB tiers article , with 50 executives and coaches ranking 35 veteran quarterbacks, Deshaun Watson was ranked 31st, with Sanders a few slots behind at 35th, last overall. Both were in the lowest tier of the rankings. The comment that jumped out about Watson was about as negative as the one on Sanders that we titled this piece with: “I don’t think he can come back,” an offensive coach said. “You do not all of a sudden get drive and desire and processing skills. He showed he had none of that with what he put on film. He’s a 5 (lowest tier ranking) at this point.” Important to note that one voter believes so much in Monken that he put Watson in Tier 2, at least that is the assumption Sando noted. The Sanders write-up is a bit longer for NY Times subscribers, but is led by the above quote from a defensive coordinator. It wasn’t all negative, however, as there are notes of hope: “If Shedeur has really invested in himself to be a professional quarterback, studying the playbook and knowing his assignments and being able to get the offense in and out of the huddle at an efficient clip, which he could not do last year, then there might be some upside,” the voter said. With one head coach actually adding praise, not just hope: “I thought he was all right, better than expected,” this coach said. “They did a good job with him of making the game simple. And I thought Shedeur played with a chip on his shoulder.” In the end, the rankings are about what the quarterbacks have done. Now, under Monken with a new offensive system, line, and set of weapons, Watson and Sanders have a chance to change the narrative about their talents. If not, 17 weeks of good sleep are coming for different defensive coordinators. What do you think about the quotes related to Watson and Sanders? Do you think they are fair or go over the top? title: Browns: Stadium updates are a bit light on substance
summary: The Cleveland Browns entered the second week of training camp by enjoying their first padded practice of the summer. So far, camp has included the first injury scare of the summer, a big-name free agent passing on a Cleveland reunion, and the annual quarterback battle that is not exactly inspiring anyone involved.  While head coach […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - DECEMBER 15: Cleveland Browns mascot Chomps performs prior to a game against the Kansas City Chiefs at Huntington Bank Field on December 15, 2024 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images The Cleveland Browns entered the second week of training camp by enjoying their first padded practice of the summer. So far, camp has included the first injury scare of the summer , a big-name free agent passing on a Cleveland reunion , and the annual quarterback battle that is not exactly inspiring anyone involved . While head coach Todd Monken and the coaching staff work to build the roster for 2026, the business side of the organization is busy building the team’s new stadium in the Cleveland suburb of Brook Park. Things have been mostly quiet in recent weeks on the stadium front, outside of the occasional nonsensical question about who the quarterback will be when the facility opens in 2029. But two items have recently come out that are of particular interest. The first is a report from Front Office Sports that, for the first time in franchise history, the Browns are expected to play their home games on an artificial turf field rather than grass. If that turns out to be true, 17 of the league’s 32 teams will be playing on artificial turf: The news comes as the long-simmering grass vs. turf debate is as active as ever thanks to the 2026 World Cup, which saw eight NFL teams temporarily replace artificial turf playing surfaces with natural grass to comply with FIFA’s requirements. The NFL Players Association used the tournament as an opportunity to advocate for more grass usage across the league. Its efforts included a coordinated social media campaign, dubbed #WorthTheCost, timed to the World Cup Final; alongside the union itself, dozens of players shared the hashtag across platforms to express their preference for grass fields. The Browns new stadium will have the “ability to accommodate grass,” … but that will likely only happen if and when the venue hosts soccer matches. Except the Browns haven’t actually announced a decision yet on the playing surface of the new stadium. Turns out the story from Front Office Sports is based on a standard Pro Football Talk post that doesn’t really say anything substantial or new. And the PFT report appears to be based on a May 5 article from cleveland.com that cites an unnamed club spokesperson who says artificial turf is “very likely.” Got all that? Good, let’s move on. The second item involves just how much fans will pay for the privilege of watching the Browns in Brook Park. During last week’s media session at training camp, owner Jimmy Haslam was asked about the possibility of fans experiencing “sticker shock” over the cost of Personal Seat Licenses, but Haslam said the pricing structure is still a work in progress : “I’m not sure who said that. We actually had a meeting on it today, and I can unequivocally say this: we have made no decisions on pricing for PSLs or tickets. We have a lot of work to do. I can tell you this — probably our number one overarching goal is to have as many affordable tickets as we can, because we’ve got great fans and they deserve it.” So what have we learned today? The Brook Park stadium might have artificial turf for football games and might have the “ability to accommodate grass,” unless it does not. In which case, the Browns will be playing indoors but on natural grass. There has been no decision made on how much tickets will be to watch the Browns, but the “goal” is to make sure an unknown will be affordable. We now return you to the training camp quarterback battle, already in progress.

(Photo by Tim Warner/UFL/Getty Images) | Getty Images A day after the Cleveland Browns were spurned by DE Jadeveon Clowney , GM Andrew Berry is right back on the transaction wire, adding a defender. On Monday, before the start of Week 2 of training camp practice , Berry and the Browns added DT Travis Bell to the roster and waived UDFA RB TJ Harden from the 90-man roster. Harden was among 12 undrafted free agents that Cleveland signed at the start of the offseason . The SMU star was “ an absolute tank in the ACC last season ” and seemed to have a chance to make the team’s 53-man roster with his pass-catching ability . The Browns didn’t see enough out of him to carry him even into the second week of training camp. Bell was a seventh-round selection by the Chicago Bears in 2023. He played two games with the Atlanta Falcons and last year in the UFL, as well as spending time on the Minnesota Vikings roster. While his NFL stats are limited (2 tackles in 2 games), Bell produced in the UFL with 39 tackles, six tackles for loss, a sack, a forced fumble, and a fumble recovery in 12 games for the Louisville Kings.

title: Shedeur Sanders, Deshaun Watson: What is best for the Browns?
summary: The offseason is officially over. As of now, all 32 teams have reported for training camp. The Cleveland Browns started their 2026 campaign last week when the team practiced for the first time under 1st-year head coach Todd Monken. This offseason, the team underwent multiple changes, but the one that everyone will pay close attention […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - JUNE 03: Deshaun Watson #4 of the Cleveland Browns talks with Shedeur Sanders #2 during the Cleveland Browns OTA Offseason Workouts at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on June 03, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images The offseason is officially over. As of now, all 32 teams have reported for training camp. The Cleveland Browns started their 2026 campaign last week when the team practiced for the first time under 1st-year head coach Todd Monken. This offseason, the team underwent multiple changes, but the one that everyone will pay close attention to is the quarterback situation . Deshaun Watson will try to salvage his football career, while Shedeur Sanders will try to prove he can be a long-term starter in the NFL, while Dillon Gabriel and Taylen Green are also on the depth chart. The last time Watson played, the tape he put up was atrocious. As for Sanders, the tape wasn’t great; he showed small flashes, but it wasn’t enough to outweigh the bad. Watson or Sanders will get a fair opportunity to win the job, but which quarterback will the team benefit from if they were to get the nod? GM Andrew Berry and Monken both have said it’s all about production , but will the decision be more nuanced than that? For Watson, it’s his last chance to prove he can play in the NFL. Since being traded to the Browns in a blockbuster deal, he hasn’t been anything close to the Pro Bowl play we saw during his tenure with the Houston Texans. An argument can be made that Watson’s first full year as the starter, after missing half of the season due to his suspension the year prior, showed signs of competency. The layoff was evident, but as the 2023 season went on, Watson showed signs of the old Watson at times. However, injuries hampered the QB relatively quickly; then he suffered a season-ending shoulder injury, but the team managed to get to the postseason despite that. Watson came back in 2024, but he was a shell of himself before tearing his Achilles. His decision-making looked worse, his athleticism began to dip, and his arm strength started to diminish. Watson didn’t play the entire 2025 season as he recovered from his Achilles tear. In terms of benefits, Cleveland gets little to no benefit starting Watson mainly due to the fact that the team is in year two of a rebuild. If winning games was the priority, and Watson won the job by a decent margin, his starting would make sense. From a personal standpoint, Watson has a lot he can benefit from. If the veteran QB goes out there and puts up adequate tape, it’s possible he can get another contract for another team, as the Browns will likely move on from Watson no matter what. It won’t be the contract he wants, but it’s better than being out of the league entirely. Sanders is entering Year 2 of his tenure in Cleveland. The young phenom, who was taken in the 5th round, is probably the most polarizing figure that is on the Browns. In terms of his popularity, he is probably the most popular player on the team for reasons that aren’t football-related. Sanders is active in the community. Sanders’ play on the field didn’t inspire much confidence in most fans and analysts, but a majority of the fans saw something the Browns can work with. As a whole, Cleveland’s offense was abysmal last season, but Sanders didn’t do enough to make the offense look better. Sanders struggled playing within the structure of the offense, held the ball too long, and often made poor decisions. It’s well documented that the Browns viewed Sanders as a project, but due to quarterback Dillon Gabriel suffering a concussion at home against the Baltimore Ravens, Sanders was thrust into the spotlight. If Sanders were to win the starting job, he would have to prove that he is capable of being a starter in the NFL for the long haul. Teams rarely commit to a 5th-round pick, and Sanders is no exception. The Browns have two 1st-round picks in this upcoming NFL draft, and the team would spend a pick on a quarterback if the opportunity presents itself. Sanders can benefit from playing with a better offensive supporting cast, but he has to show growth for the Browns to commit long-term to him. Big picture, it is in Cleveland’s best interest if Sanders (or Gabriel for that matter) wins the starting job in 2026. What do you think should matter for the Browns QB decision? Is it just 2026 and “production,” or should the long-term view take an important role? Join the conversation! title: Cowboys news: Secondary steals the show in 1st padded practice
summary: Practice Points: Takeaways from first padded practice – Staff, DallasCowboys.com The Cowboys secondary looked pretty good once the pads came on. The Land Shark Cometh – Cobie Durant’s momentum over the first three practices ramped up even more on Monday, when the pads came on. His coverage is some of the best on the Cowboys’ defense […]
full_text: Jul 29, 2026; Oxnard, CA, USA; Dallas Cowboys cornerback Cobie Durant (2) at training camp at River Ridge Playing Fields. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Practice Points: Takeaways from first padded practice – Staff, DallasCowboys.com The Cowboys secondary looked pretty good once the pads came on. The Land Shark Cometh – Cobie Durant’s momentum over the first three practices ramped up even more on Monday, when the pads came on. His coverage is some of the best on the Cowboys’ defense and, on one play in particular, he showed Dak Prescott what he can do. Prescott dropped back in the red zone and threw a ball under duress to CeeDee Lamb, who was in good enough position to make the catch after he broke outside; but Durant peeled off of his original coverage, readjusted and jumped the route to make an acrobatic interception that had Christian Parker smiling. – (Patrik Walker) Bringin’ the Wood – On the first day of pads, you wouldn’t expect anything other than someone named “Julius Wood” to have a physical practice. Just an hour before, his head coach Brian Schottenheimer mentioned Wood as being active and making the safety position rather deep. And then in practice, he had several big pops, jarring the ball loose on a pass during the team drills and he also wasn’t afraid to come up in run support. Also, Caleb Downs had a few run stops as well. But Wood is a guy trying to get noticed – and he did that Monday. – (Nick Eatman) Revel In the Moment – What Shavon Revel is experiencing in his second NFL training camp is the definition of iron sharpens iron. Before today, CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens were narrowly inching him out to make big plays but, in the first padded practice, Revel had several PBUs and even wagged his finger at Pickens on one of them. Going against two of the best in the league combines with Revel being fully healthy to make for what might be a return to peak form once witnessed at ECU only two short seasons ago. (Patrik Walker) Downs to Business – Caleb Downs may not always make the flashy, highlight plays all the time for a defensive back, but he makes big plays that the offense feels well afterwards. That was the case today, as Downs had a teach-tape run fill against the first team offense, as he was waiting in the gap when Jaydon Blue was trying to get through it. Downs’ work at the line of scrimmage is one that popped up a lot at Ohio State, and has done so in flashes during his first NFL training camp with the Cowboys too. He’s also been active around the ball in coverage, as Downs had a near interception today off a pass that DaRon Bland deflected into the air. – (Tommy Yarrish) Cowboys cornerbacks get off to a hot start at first padded practice – Matthew Holleran, Blogging The Boys The Cowboys wide receiver versus cornerback battles have been fiery in Oxnard. If today’s practice is any indication of how the group is going to perform during the regular season, Cowboys fans are going to be very pleased. The trio of Bland, Durant, and Revel all had great showings during today’s padded practice. Bland and Durant started the day off by both recording a PBU against the first-team offense. Dallas’ starting cornerback group continued to perform well as practice wore on, highlighted by Durant intercepting Dak Prescott in the red zone. It’s hard to overstate how much Dallas’ postseason hopes rely on their starting cornerback trio not just staying on the field, but playing well while doing so. There’s no way around it; last year was ugly for both Daron Bland and Shavon Revel. The Cowboys showed plenty of support for the duo this offseason, but now it’s time for both players to prove Dallas right for believing in them. Durant will be a true x-factor for Dallas’ defense. If he can play a vital role in Dallas’ defense alongside Bland and Revel, the Cowboys have a chance to have an above-average secondary. Let’s hope Dallas’ cornerback group continues to play like they did on Monday afternoon moving forward. Dak Prescott already noticed a big difference from this year’s Dallas Cowboys defense only a few days into training camp – Mauricio Rodriguez, A to Z Sports A noticeable improvement from the Cowboys defense under Christian Parker, straight from their highest-paid player and starting quarterback. That hasn’t stopped Prescott from noticing a big difference from the Cowboys defense he’s facing every day. And with the Cowboys set to wear pads for the first time on Monday, it’s only fair to say the battle between an elite offense and a rebuilt defense is only beginning. This summer, Prescott is facing the fourth Cowboys defensive coordinator in camp since 2023. What has he noticed from the new-look defense led by 34-year-old defensive coordinator Christian Parker? “A defense that is communicating,” Prescott told reporters last week. “A defense that takes a lot of pride in what they do in each and every one of their calls, taking pride in playing with one another.” For Parker, who wants to run a defense that is multiple and capable to adjust on the fly, communication is crucial. In order to do that, players have to be loud. So far, Prescott is impressed with the decibels coming from the other side of the line of scrimmage. “When we motion, you can hear how loud they are and them getting to the right fits or calls that they need to make, and just challenging us,” Prescott added. Rookie Caleb Downs Sets Lofty Goal for Cowboys’ Defense During NFL Season – Timothy Rapp, Bleacher Report Caleb Downs’ high expectations for himself as a rookie can be found all throughout the Cowboys defense right now. “To be dominant,” he told Jon Machota of The Athletic when asked about his expectations for the defense in the 2026 season. “That’s what I’ve thought about with every defense I’ve been on. And we have the talent to do it, to dominate every offense that we go against.” In 2025, the Cowboys gave up an NFL-worst 251.5 passing yards and 30.1 points per game. Many pointed to the questionable decision to trade superstar edge-rusher Micah Parsons before the season, though the secondary was porous at best. But attempts were made to rectify the pass defense this offseason. The Cowboys traded for edge-rusher Rashan Gary, filling the void left by Parsons a year ago, and drafted pass-rusher Malachi Lawrence at No. 26 overall (one of five defensive players the team drafted in the first four rounds). The secondary was bolstered in free agency with the signings of safety Jalen Thompson and cornerback Cobie Durant. And most importantly, Downs was the No. 11 overall pick and is already being utilized as both a safety and nickelback. Here’s what Cowboys former 5th-round pick must do to earn game snaps – Reid Hanson, The Cowboys Wire With buzz about the passing game and pass defense still dominating all the headlines from Oxnard, how about another check in on the RB2 competition and Jaydon Blue? It’s no secret the Dallas Cowboys hope Jaydon Blue takes over the RB2 spot behind starter Javonte Williams. The former Texas running back has game-changing speed and big-play ability that would complement Williams’ physical style well. He was a complementary back in college, and he’s tabbed to be a complementary back in the NFL. It’s a match made in heaven. Yet, Blue’s first season in Dallas proved to be a total disappointment. Critical aspects of the job fell on deaf ears and aside from a 16-carry performance in Week 18, Blue was basically a nonfactor in his rookie year. Hope springs eternal in Year 2 for Blue. After saying the right things in the offseason and doing the right things early in training camp, Blue is back on track to be that RB2 he was always meant to be. But there’s one task, one unavoidable quality he has to prove before he can officially be given second-fiddle designation in Dallas, and that’s pass protection. The NFL game is one of chess strategization. Offensive coordinators are trying to outsmart defensive…

The first few practices of camp, while exciting, are always glorified seven-on-seven drills. Today, that changed in a big way. For the first time in Oxnard, real football is finally back, as the Dallas Cowboys held their first padded practice of the summer this afternoon. When the pads go on, the intensity level skyrockets. We’ve seen plenty of memorable moments over the years during Dallas’ first few padded practices, and it’s almost certain we’ll get a few more this week. Even though the Cowboys won’t face anyone other than themselves until the Rams joint practice in over a week, the first few padded practices of training camp are always a treat. Players ratchet up the intensity in a big way, and we get our first true look at which guys can separate themselves from the pack. With Dallas’ offense not featuring many new faces, they figured to have the leg up in the first padded practice of camp. Surprisingly, it was the defense that stole the show early on, including an impressive showing from the Cowboys’ cornerback group. You could make a legitimate argument that how Dallas’ cornerback group performs this season (health aside) will have as much of an impact on the team as any other position outside of quarterback and wide receiver. The Cowboys are relying on Daron Bland and Shavon Revel Jr. to bounce back in a big way while also needing a solid year out of free agent acquisition Cobie Durant. If today’s practice is any indication of how the group is going to perform during the regular season, Cowboys fans are going to be very pleased. The trio of Bland, Durant, and Revel all had great showings during today’s padded practice. Bland and Durant started the day off by both recording a PBU against the first-team offense. Cobie Durant tight coverage and a PBU against CeeDee Lamb. pic.twitter.com/u3NTgg9AWe — Joseph Hoyt (@JoeJHoyt) August 3, 2026 DaRon Bland and Caleb Downs with tight coverage here for the PBU. pic.twitter.com/QvcfgaRiQ1 — Joseph Hoyt (@JoeJHoyt) August 3, 2026 Dallas’ starting cornerback group continued to perform well as practice wore on, highlighted by Durant intercepting Dak Prescott in the red zone. Cobie Durant INT pic.twitter.com/uUbF9wN64M — Jon Machota (@jonmachota) August 3, 2026 CeeDee Lamb got one on Shavon Revel in space on the rep prior, but Revel almost had him one here to get his lick back. #Cowboys pic.twitter.com/BaekVyE5NK — Patrik [No C] Walker (@VoiceOfTheStar) August 3, 2026 Shavon Revel with good coverage here. Starting to stack some reps pic.twitter.com/FsIaJeGQ3l — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) August 3, 2026 It’s hard to overstate how much Dallas’ postseason hopes rely on their starting cornerback trio not just staying on the field, but playing well while doing so. There’s no way around it; last year was ugly for both Daron Bland and Shavon Revel. The Cowboys showed plenty of support for the duo this offseason, but now it’s time for both players to prove Dallas right for believing in them. Durant will be a true x-factor for Dallas’ defense. If he can play a vital role in Dallas’ defense alongside Bland and Revel, the Cowboys have a chance to have an above-average secondary. Let’s hope Dallas’ cornerback group continues to play like they did on Monday afternoon moving forward.

title: Cowboys countdown to kickoff: Top 100 iconic games – Day 41
summary: It is Day 41 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like […]
full_text: (Original Caption) Miami, Florida: Baltimore's Roy Jefferson (87) is dragged to the ground by Dallas' Lee Roy Jordan (55) in the Super Bowl V. It is Day 41 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. Welcome everyone to Day 41 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff, when we revisit one of the most painful and historically significant losses in Cowboys history. It was Dallas’ first Super Bowl appearance and the first Super Bowl staged after the AFL-NFL merger formally created the AFC and NFC. The Cowboys led for almost the entire afternoon, forced seven Baltimore turnovers, but the end result was heartbreaking for all of Cowboys nation. Sunday, January 17, 1971 — 2:00 p.m. ET Miami Orange Bowl, Miami, Florida Final Score: Baltimore Colts 16, Dallas Cowboys 13 Dallas opened the scoring after Chuck Howley intercepted Johnny Unitas and returned the ball into Colts territory. The Cowboys could not reach the end zone, but Mike Clark made a 14-yard field goal for a 3-0 lead. Clark added another field goal from 30 yards early in the second quarter, giving Dallas a 6-0 advantage in a game that had already become physical, disjointed and filled with mistakes. Baltimore’s first touchdown came on one of the strangest scoring plays in Super Bowl history. Unitas threw high and behind Eddie Hinton, the ball glanced off Hinton’s hands and was touched by Cowboys cornerback Mel Renfro before dropping to tight end John Mackey. Mackey caught the ricochet and ran 75 yards for a touchdown. Dallas blocked O’Brien’s extra point, keeping the score tied at 6-6. The Cowboys reclaimed the lead before halftime. Craig Morton completed a seven-yard touchdown pass to Duane Thomas, and Clark’s extra point put Dallas ahead 13-6. Baltimore then drove to the Cowboys’ goal line in the final minutes of the half, but the Doomsday Defense stopped Norm Bulaich three times near the end zone before forcing an incompletion on fourth down. Dallas carried its seven-point lead into halftime. Neither team scored in the third quarter, but the turnovers continued. Dallas’ defense repeatedly gave the offense chances to extend the lead, while the Cowboys failed to take advantage. Howley intercepted replacement quarterback Earl Morrall in the end zone on the opening play of the fourth quarter, preserving the 13-6 advantage and giving him his second interception of the afternoon. Baltimore then produced another bizarre sequence. Sam Havrilak took a handoff on a planned flea-flicker but was unable to lateral the ball back to Morrall, so he threw downfield instead. Hinton caught it and headed toward the end zone, only for Cornell Green to strip him from behind. The loose ball bounced through the end zone for a touchback, seemingly giving Dallas another escape. The relief lasted only three plays. Morton’s pass was deflected and intercepted by Colts safety Rick Volk, who returned it to the Dallas three-yard line. Tom Nowatzke scored from two yards out shortly afterward, and O’Brien’s extra point tied the game at 13 with 7:35 remaining. The Cowboys still had an opportunity to win. They took possession near midfield with less than two minutes remaining, but a holding penalty against Ralph Neely pushed Dallas backward. Facing second-and-35, Morton threw toward Dan Reeves. The pass went off Reeves’ hands and into the arms of Baltimore linebacker Mike Curtis, who returned the interception to the Dallas 28 with 1:09 left. Baltimore ran two plays to improve the position, and O’Brien came on for a 32-yard field goal. The rookie kicker made it with five seconds remaining, giving the Colts their first lead of the entire game. Dallas’ final desperation pass was intercepted, and Baltimore completed a 16-13 comeback that left Cowboys defensive tackle Bob Lilly so frustrated that he threw his helmet far downfield after the final whistle. This game belongs on the countdown because it represents the deepest pain of the Cowboys’ rise from expansion team to NFL power. Dallas had been close before, but Super Bowl V put the franchise within seconds of its first championship before another late mistake took it away. The defeat also strengthened the perception that the Cowboys could reach the biggest stage but could not finish. But that was soon to change. #Cowboys vs #Colts 1971 Super Bowl V Final Score: Baltimore Colts 16, Dallas Cowboys 13 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/lO6goWZJME — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) August 3, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game Super Bowl V became known as the “Blunder Bowl” because the teams combined for 11 turnovers. Baltimore committed seven, while Dallas turned it over four times. Dallas has a plethora of others guys that are making waves as well under the California sun. Let’s take a look at three players that have improved the most since camp started. Jaishawn Barham Barham was taken in the third round back in April, and he’s battling for early playing time at the linebacker spot. Learning curves are expected in these situations, but Barham is looking like seasoned pro in a short amount of time. Whether it’s been against the run or the pass, Barham’s instincts and processing ability have been on full display. At Michigan, Barham played both linebacker and edge. He’ll be asked to due some of both in Dallas as well. That type of versatility makes him a great fit for what Christian Parker wants to do, and if he keeps that up when the pads come on, veteran Dee Winters will have some serious competition at middle linebacker. Yes, Barham is a rookie, but he’s taken a leap already. He’s adapted to the NFL very well so far, and the eyes on him will only increase once he’s in pads. Blue was limited to only just five game appearances as a rookie in 2025, but he’s well on his way to passing that in his second year if this type of progression continues during camp and the preseason.
